title.raw: 卷67 崔光 Volume 67: Cui Guang

sentences.zh: 崔光，本名孝伯，字長仁，高祖賜名焉，東清河鄃人也。

translations.literal: Cui Guang, original name Xiaobo, courtesy name Changren, the High Emperor bestowed the name upon him; he was a native of Fu in Eastern Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang, whose original name was Xiaobo and whose courtesy name was Changren, received his given name from Emperor Gaozu. He came from Fu in Eastern Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖曠，從慕容德南渡河，居青州之時水。

translations.literal: His grandfather Kuang followed Murong De in crossing the river south and settled at Shishui in Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Kuang had followed Murong De south across the Yellow River and settled at Shishui in Qing province.

sentences.zh: 慕容氏滅，仕劉義隆為樂陵太守。

translations.literal: When the Murong clan was destroyed, he served Liu Yilong as prefect of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Murong regime, he entered the service of Liu Yilong and became prefect of Leling.

sentences.zh: 父靈延，劉駿龍驤將軍、長廣太守，與劉彧冀州刺史崔道固共拒國軍。

translations.literal: His father Lingyan was a Dragon-Prancing General under Liu Jun and prefect of Changguang; together with Cui Daogu, regional inspector of Ji province under Liu Yu, he resisted the imperial army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lingyan had served Liu Jun as Dragon-Prancing General and prefect of Changguang, and together with Cui Daogu, Liu Yu's inspector of Ji province, he had resisted the Northern Wei forces.

sentences.zh: 慕容白曜之平三齊，光年十七，隨父徙代。

translations.literal: When Murong Baiyao pacified the Three Qi, Guang was seventeen and moved to Dai with his father.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Baiyao conquered the Three Qi, Guang was seventeen and accompanied his father in resettling at Dai.

sentences.zh: 家貧好學，晝耕夜誦，傭書以養父母。

translations.literal: His family was poor but he loved learning; by day he plowed and by night he recited texts, hiring himself out to copy books to support his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family was poor, he was devoted to learning. He farmed by day and studied by night, earning his keep by copying books so that he could support his parents.

sentences.zh: 太和六年，拜中書博士，轉著作郎，與祕書丞李彪參撰國書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taihe he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat, then transferred to Gentleman of the Writing Office, and together with Secretariat Director Li Biao he helped compile the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Taihe era he was appointed Erudite of the Secretariat, then promoted to Gentleman of the Writing Office, where he joined Secretariat Director Li Biao in compiling the dynastic history.

sentences.zh: 遷中書侍郎、給事黃門侍郎，甚為高祖所知待。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, and was greatly known and favored by the High Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to Secretariat Gentleman and Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Yellow Gate, positions in which he won the High Emperor's deep trust and favor.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「孝伯之才，浩浩如黃河東注，固今日之文宗也。

translations.literal: He often said: "Xiaobo's talent flows vast as the Yellow River pouring eastward; he is truly the literary patriarch of our age.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often remarked, "Xiaobo's talent pours forth like the Yellow River rushing east — he is truly the master of letters in our time.

sentences.zh: 」以參贊遷都之謀，賜爵朝陽子，拜散騎常侍，黃門、著作如故，又兼太子少傅。

translations.literal: " For assisting in the plan to move the capital he was granted the title Marquis of Chaoyang, appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, and retained his Yellow Gate and Writing Office posts; he also concurrently served as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: " For his part in planning the capital transfer he was ennobled as Marquis of Chaoyang and appointed Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry, while retaining his posts at the Yellow Gate and Writing Office. He was also made Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼侍中、使持節，為陝西大使，巡方省察，所經述敍古事，因而賦詩三十八篇。

translations.literal: Soon, retaining his original office, he concurrently served as Palace Attendant with credentials bearing the staff of authority as Grand Ambassador to Shaanxi, touring the regions on inspection; wherever he passed he narrated ancient events and composed thirty-eight poems.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was given the additional posts of Palace Attendant and commissioner bearing the staff of authority, and sent as Grand Ambassador to the western Shaanxi region to tour and inspect the provinces. Along the route he recounted historical events at each place he visited and composed thirty-eight poems.

sentences.zh: 還，仍兼侍中，以謀謨之功，進爵為伯。

translations.literal: On his return he still held the concurrent post of Palace Attendant, and for his achievements in planning and counsel he was advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned he continued to serve concurrently as Palace Attendant, and for his contributions to state planning he was promoted from marquis to count.

sentences.zh: 初，光與李彪共撰國書，太和之末，彪解著作，專以史事任光。

translations.literal: At first Guang and Li Biao jointly compiled the national history; at the end of Taihe, Biao was relieved of the Writing Office post and Guang alone was charged with historical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guang and Li Biao had worked together on the dynastic history. At the end of the Taihe era Biao was removed from the Writing Office, and the entire charge of historical compilation was placed on Guang alone.

sentences.zh: 彪尋以罪廢。

translations.literal: Biao was soon dismissed for a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Biao was soon stripped of office for a crime.

sentences.zh: 世宗居諒闇，彪上表求成魏書，詔許之，彪遂以白衣於祕書省著述。

translations.literal: While the Shizong Emperor was in mourning seclusion, Biao submitted a memorial requesting permission to complete the Book of Wei; the edict approved it, and Biao thereupon composed at the Secretariat in plain dress.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Shizong was in mourning seclusion, Biao petitioned for permission to complete the Book of Wei. The throne approved, and Biao was allowed to write at the Secretariat as a private citizen.

sentences.zh: 光雖領史官，以彪意在專功，表解侍中、著作以讓彪，世宗不許。

translations.literal: Although Guang headed the historiographical office, seeing that Biao intended to monopolize the achievement he memorialized to resign his posts as Palace Attendant and Writing Office director in Biao's favor; the Shizong Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Although Guang still headed the historiographical office, he saw that Biao wished to claim sole credit for the work. He therefore petitioned to resign as Palace Attendant and director of the Writing Office in Biao's favor, but Emperor Shizong refused.

sentences.zh: 遷太常卿，領齊州大中正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies and concurrently served as chief rectifier of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of Ceremonies and appointed chief rectifier of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 正始元年夏，有典事史元顯獻四足四翼雞，詔散騎侍郎趙邕以問光，光表答曰：

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Zhengshi, a clerk of current affairs named Yuan Xian presented a chicken with four legs and four wings; an edict ordered Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Zhao Yong to consult Guang, and Guang replied in a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Zhengshi, a clerk of current affairs named Yuan Xian presented a chicken with four legs and four wings. The throne ordered Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Zhao Yong to seek Guang's interpretation, and Guang replied in a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣謹按：漢書五行志：宣帝黃龍元年，未央殿路軨中，雌雞化為雄，毛變而不鳴不將，無距。

translations.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: in the Treatise on the Five Phases in the Book of Han, in the first year of Huanglong under Emperor Xuan, within the carriage-rail of Weiyang Palace a hen transformed into a cock; its feathers changed but it did not crow or lead the flock, and had no spurs.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant respectfully observes that the Treatise on the Five Phases in the Book of Han records that in the first year of Huanglong under Emperor Xuan, a hen in the carriage-rail of Weiyang Palace transformed into a rooster. Its plumage changed, but it neither crowed nor led the flock, and it had no spurs.

sentences.zh: 元帝初元中，丞相府史家雌雞伏子，漸化為雄，冠距鳴將。

translations.literal: In the Chuyuan era under Emperor Yuan, at the home of a clerk in the Chancellor's office a hen brooding eggs gradually transformed into a cock, with comb, spurs, crowing, and leading the flock.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuyuan era under Emperor Yuan, a hen brooding eggs in the household of a clerk in the chancellor's office gradually transformed into a rooster, complete with comb and spurs, and began to crow and lead the flock.

sentences.zh: 永光中，有獻雄雞生角。

translations.literal: In the Yongguang era someone presented a cock that grew horns.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongguang era someone presented a rooster that had grown horns.

sentences.zh: 劉向以為雞者小畜，主司時起居，小臣執事為政之象也。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang held that the chicken is a minor domestic animal governing seasonal routine, and is an emblem of petty officials holding power in government.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang interpreted these signs to mean that the chicken, as a minor domestic animal charged with marking the seasons, symbolized petty officials seizing control of government affairs.

sentences.zh: 言小臣將乘君之威，以害政事，猶石顯也。

translations.literal: This meant petty officials would ride the ruler's authority to harm government affairs, like Shi Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Such omens meant that minor officials would exploit the ruler's authority to corrupt governance — as Shi Xian had done.

sentences.zh: 竟寧元年，石顯伏辜，此其效也。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingning, Shi Xian was punished for his crimes — this was the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingning, Shi Xian was executed for his crimes — the omen had found its fulfillment.

sentences.zh: 靈帝光和元年，南宮寺雌雞欲化為雄，一身毛皆似雄，但頭冠尚未變。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guanghe under Emperor Ling, at Nangong Temple a hen was transforming into a cock; its entire body resembled a male's, but the comb on its head had not yet changed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guanghe under Emperor Ling, a hen at Nangong Temple was in the process of transforming into a rooster. Its entire body had taken on a male appearance, but the comb on its head had not yet changed.

sentences.zh: 詔以問議郎蔡邕，邕對曰：「貌之不恭，則有雞禍。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Consultation Gentleman Cai Yong questioned; Yong replied: "When deportment lacks reverence, there is the calamity of the chicken.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Consultation Gentleman Cai Yong to interpret the omen. Yong replied, "When deportment lacks reverence, the calamity of the chicken appears.

sentences.zh: 臣竊推之，頭為元首，人君之象也，今雞一身已變，未至於頭，而上知之，是將有其事，而不遂成之象也。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to infer: the head is the chief member and the image of the ruler; now the chicken's body has changed but not yet its head, and the ruler above is aware of it — this is the sign of something about to happen that will not be fully accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant ventures this interpretation: the head is the chief member and symbolizes the ruler. The chicken's body has already changed, but not its head, and the ruler above has taken notice. This is the sign of a threat that has begun but will not reach completion.

sentences.zh: 若應之不精，政無所改，頭冠或成，為患滋大。

translations.literal: If the response is not precise and government undergoes no reform, the comb may yet form and the harm grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: If the omen is not heeded with precision and no reforms are made, the comb may yet fully form and the calamity grow far worse.

sentences.zh: 」是後張角作亂，稱「黃巾賊」，遂破壞四方，疲於賦役，民多叛者。

translations.literal: " After this Zhang Jiao raised rebellion, calling himself the "Yellow Turban bandit," and destroyed the four quarters; the people, exhausted by taxes and corvée, rebelled in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Zhang Jiao rose in rebellion under the banner of the Yellow Turbans, throwing the empire into chaos. The people, worn down by taxes and forced labor, rose in rebellion across the land.

sentences.zh: 上不改政，遂至天下大亂。

translations.literal: The ruler did not reform his policies, and thus the realm fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Because the ruler made no reforms, the empire descended into utter chaos.

sentences.zh: 今之雞狀雖與漢不同，而其應頗相類矣。

translations.literal: Though the present chicken's form differs from Han times, its correspondence is quite similar.
translations.idiomatic: Although the present chicken's form differs from those recorded in Han times, the correspondence of omen and outcome is strikingly similar.

sentences.zh: 向、邕並博達之士，考物驗事，信而有證，誠可畏也。

translations.literal: Xiang and Yong were both broadly learned scholars; examining things and testing events, their words were trustworthy and substantiated — truly something to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Both Liu Xiang and Cai Yong were scholars of vast learning whose interpretations of natural signs proved trustworthy and well substantiated. Their example is truly sobering.

sentences.zh: 臣以邕言推之，翅足眾多，亦羣下相扇助之象，雛而未大，脚羽差小，亦其勢尚微，易制御也。

translations.literal: Your servant, extrapolating from Yong's words, infers that the numerous wings and feet also signify subordinates inciting and aiding one another; being a chick not yet grown, with feet and feathers somewhat small, its force is still slight and easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: Extrapolating from Yong's analysis, your servant infers that the numerous wings and feet signify subordinates inciting one another to rebellion. Yet because this creature is still a chick, with small feet and immature feathers, the threat remains slight and can still be brought under control.

sentences.zh: 臣聞災異之見，皆所以示吉凶，明君覩之而懼，乃能招福；

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the appearance of disasters and anomalies is meant to show good fortune or ill; a wise ruler who sees them and is afraid can thereby draw down blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that disasters and anomalies appear precisely to signal fortune or misfortune. A wise ruler who sees them and is moved to fear can thereby draw down blessing.

sentences.zh: 闇主視之彌慢，所用致禍。

translations.literal: a dark ruler who views them with growing indifference thereby brings calamity upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: A benighted ruler who greets them with growing indifference brings calamity upon himself.

sentences.zh: 詩、書、春秋、秦、漢之事多矣，此陛下所觀者也。

translations.literal: The affairs recorded in the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, Qin, and Han are many — these are what Your Majesty may observe.
translations.idiomatic: The histories of the Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, Qin, and Han offer abundant examples of this — examples that Your Majesty may consult at will.

sentences.zh: 今或有自賤而貴，關預政事，殆亦前代君房之匹比者。

translations.literal: Now there may be those who rise from low estate to high rank and interfere in government affairs — perhaps comparable to Junfang of former ages.
translations.idiomatic: At present there may be men who have risen from humble origins to high office and now meddle in state affairs — men perhaps comparable to Shi Xian of former times.

sentences.zh: 南境死亡千計，白骨橫野，存有酷恨之痛，歿為怨傷之魂。

translations.literal: On the southern frontier deaths number in the thousands; white bones lie across the fields; the living bear the pain of bitter hatred, the dead become resentful wounded spirits.
translations.idiomatic: On the southern frontier deaths run into the thousands, and white bones lie strewn across the fields. The living endure the agony of bitter hatred, and the dead become vengeful spirits.

sentences.zh: 義陽屯師，盛夏未返；

translations.literal: Troops are encamped at Yiyang and have not returned even in midsummer;
translations.idiomatic: Troops encamped at Yiyang have not returned even in the height of summer;

sentences.zh: 荊蠻狡猾，征人淹次。

translations.literal: the Jing barbarians are cunning, and the expeditionary forces are long detained.
translations.idiomatic: the Jing tribes are cunning, and the expeditionary forces are long detained.

sentences.zh: 東州轉輸，往多無還；

translations.literal: transport convoys from the eastern provinces mostly do not return;
translations.idiomatic: Transport convoys from the eastern provinces mostly never return;

sentences.zh: 百姓困窮，絞縊以殞。

translations.literal: the common people are destitute and hang themselves to die.
translations.idiomatic: the common people, driven to destitution, hang themselves to escape their misery.

sentences.zh: 北方霜降，蠶婦輟事。

translations.literal: In the north frost has fallen and silkworm-raising women have ceased their work.
translations.idiomatic: In the north the frost has already fallen, and women who tend silkworms have been forced to abandon their work.

sentences.zh: 羣生憔悴，莫甚於今。

translations.literal: All living things are withered — never worse than now.
translations.idiomatic: All living creatures are withered and spent — never has the suffering been worse than now.

sentences.zh: 此亦賈誼哭歎，谷永切諫之時。

translations.literal: This is also the time when Jia Yi wept and sighed and Gu Yong offered urgent remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: This is the very hour that calls for the weeping lament of a Jia Yi and the urgent remonstrance of a Gu Yong.

sentences.zh: 司寇行戮，君為之不舉，陛下為民父母，所宜矜恤。

translations.literal: When the Minister of Crime carries out executions, the ruler refrains from feasting; Your Majesty is father and mother to the people and ought to show compassion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Minister of Crime carries out executions, the ruler suspends his feasts out of respect for life. Your Majesty is father and mother to the people and ought to show them compassion.

sentences.zh: 國重戎戰，用兵猶火，內外怨弊，易以亂離。

translations.literal: The state relies heavily on military campaigns; using troops is like using fire — resentment and exhaustion within and without make disorder and separation easy.
translations.idiomatic: The state relies heavily on military campaigns, and the use of arms is like playing with fire. Resentment and exhaustion within and without make rebellion and disintegration all too easy.

sentences.zh: 陛下縱欲忽天下，豈不仰念太祖取之艱難，先帝經營劬勞也。

translations.literal: Even if Your Majesty wishes to disregard the realm, should you not look up and recall how hard the Founding Emperor won it and how the late emperor toiled in its governance?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty were inclined to disregard the realm, should you not reflect on how arduously the Founding Emperor won the empire and how exhaustingly the late emperor labored to govern it?

sentences.zh: 誠願陛下留聰明之鑒，警天地之意，禮處左右，節其貴越。

translations.literal: Your servant sincerely wishes Your Majesty to retain your discerning intelligence, heed the intent of Heaven and Earth, treat those at your side with propriety, and restrain their extravagant rank.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant earnestly prays that Your Majesty will keep your discerning intelligence alert, heed the warnings of Heaven and Earth, treat those at your side with proper ceremony, and restrain their extravagant advancement.

sentences.zh: 往者鄧通、董賢之盛，愛之正所以害之。

translations.literal: In the past the grandeur of Deng Tong and Dong Xian — loving them was precisely how to harm them.
translations.idiomatic: In ages past the favor lavished on Deng Tong and Dong Xian ended by destroying them — excessive love is itself a form of harm.

sentences.zh: 又躬饗加罕，宴宗或闕，時應親肅郊廟，延敬諸父。

translations.literal: Moreover, personally attend sacrifices more rarely, and banquets for the imperial clan are sometimes omitted; at times you should personally perform solemn rites at the suburban altars and temples and extend respect to your uncles.
translations.idiomatic: Attend sacrificial rites in person more often, and do not neglect banquets for the imperial clan. Perform solemn ceremonies at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and show due respect to your uncles.

sentences.zh: 檢訪四方，務加休息，爰發慈旨，撫賑貧瘼。

translations.literal: Inspect the four quarters, strive to grant rest, issue compassionate edicts, and comfort and relieve the destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Tour the four quarters of the realm, strive to grant the people rest, issue compassionate edicts, and bring relief to the destitute and afflicted.

sentences.zh: 簡費山池，減撤聲飲，晝存政道，夜以安身。

translations.literal: Reduce expenditures on mountain parks and ponds, cut back music and drink, keep to the path of governance by day and rest the body by night.
translations.idiomatic: Reduce expenditures on parks and pleasure grounds, cut back on music and feasting, devote the daylight hours to governance, and rest the body at night.

sentences.zh: 博釆芻蕘，進賢黜佞。

translations.literal: Broadly gather counsel even from firewood gatherers, advance the worthy and dismiss the flatterers.
translations.idiomatic: Seek counsel broadly, even from the humblest sources; promote the worthy and dismiss the flatterers.

sentences.zh: 則兆庶幸甚，妖弭慶進，禎祥集矣。

translations.literal: Then the myriad people will be greatly blessed, omens will be quelled and felicity will advance, and auspicious signs will gather.
translations.idiomatic: Then the myriad people will be greatly blessed, evil omens will be quelled, good fortune will flourish, and auspicious signs will gather.

sentences.zh: 世宗覽之，大悅。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor read it and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong read the memorial and was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 後數日，而茹皓等並以罪失伏法。

translations.literal: Several days later Ru Hao and others all lost their positions for crimes and were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days Ru Hao and his associates were all stripped of office for their crimes and executed.

sentences.zh: 於是禮光愈重，加撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guang was honored all the more, and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was thereafter held in even greater esteem and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，光表曰：「去二十八日，有物出于太極之西序，敕以示臣，臣按其形，即莊子所謂『蒸成菌』者也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year, Guang memorialized: "On the twenty-eighth day past, something emerged in the western wing of the Taiji Hall; an edict showed it to your servant, and your servant examined its form — it is what Zhuangzi called 'vapor congealed into fungus.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year Guang memorialized: "Twenty-eight days ago something appeared in the western wing of the Taiji Hall. Your Majesty showed it to your servant, and upon examining its form your servant recognized it as what Zhuangzi called 'vapor congealed into fungus.'

sentences.zh: 又云『朝菌不終晦朔』，雍門周所稱『磨蕭斧而伐朝菌』，皆指言蒸氣鬱長，非有根種，柔脆之質，凋殞速易，不延旬月，無擬斧斤。

translations.literal: It is also said that 'morning fungus does not last out the month,' and Yongmen Zhou spoke of 'sharpening the Xiao axe to fell morning fungus' — all referring to vapor steaming and growing rank, without root or seed, of soft fragile substance, withering and perishing swiftly, not lasting ten days or a month, unworthy of axe and blade.
translations.idiomatic: The saying that 'morning fungus does not survive a full month,' and Yongmen Zhou's remark about 'sharpening the Xiao axe to fell morning fungus,' both describe vapor that steams and grows rank without root or seed — a soft, fragile thing that withers and dies quickly, lasting no more than ten days or a month, scarcely worth the stroke of an axe.

sentences.zh: 又多生墟落穢濕之地，罕起殿堂高華之所。

translations.literal: It also grows mostly in abandoned villages and foul damp places, and rarely appears in lofty splendid halls.
translations.idiomatic: Such fungus grows chiefly in abandoned villages and foul, damp places, and rarely appears in lofty, splendid halls.

sentences.zh: 今極宇崇麗，牆築工密，糞朽弗加，沾濡不及，而茲菌歘構，厥狀扶疏，誠足異也。

translations.literal: Now the utmost hall is lofty and splendid, its walls built with meticulous craft, no filth or rot added, no moisture reaching it — yet this fungus suddenly formed, its shape luxuriant; truly it is strange.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now, in this utmost hall so lofty and splendid, with walls built with meticulous craft, where no filth is added and no moisture can reach, this fungus has suddenly appeared in luxuriant form — truly a remarkable thing.

sentences.zh: 夫野木生朝，野鳥入廟，古人以為敗亡之象。

translations.literal: Wild trees growing in the court, wild birds entering the temple — the ancients took these as signs of defeat and ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Wild trees growing in the court and wild birds entering the temple — the ancients regarded these as omens of defeat and ruin.

sentences.zh: 然懼災修德者，咸致休慶，所謂家利而怪先，國興而妖豫。

translations.literal: Yet those who feared disasters and cultivated virtue all attained rest and celebration — as the saying goes, when the family is about to prosper, monsters appear first; when the state is about to rise, portents come in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those rulers who feared calamity and cultivated virtue all attained peace and prosperity — as the saying goes, when a family is about to prosper, strange signs appear first; when a state is about to flourish, portents come in advance.

sentences.zh: 是故桑穀拱庭，太戊以昌；

translations.literal: Thus when mulberry and grain arched over the court, Tai Wu prospered;
translations.idiomatic: When mulberry and grain arched over the court, King Tai Wu prospered;

sentences.zh: 雊雉集鼎，武丁用熙。

translations.literal: when a crowing pheasant perched on the cauldron, Wu Ding flourished.
translations.idiomatic: when a crowing pheasant perched on the ritual cauldron, King Wu Ding flourished.

sentences.zh: 自比鴟鵲巢于廟殿，梟鵩鳴於宮寢，菌生賓階軒坐之正，準諸往記，信可為誡。

translations.literal: Comparing with owl and magpie nesting in temple halls, owl and kite crying in palace chambers, fungus growing on the guest stair at the seat of honor — measured against past records, this can truly serve as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Compared with owls and magpies nesting in temple halls, owls and kites crying in palace chambers, and fungus growing on the guest stair at the seat of honor — measured against the records of the past, this omen can truly serve as a warning.

sentences.zh: 且南西未靜，兵革不息，郊甸之內，大旱跨時，民勞物悴，莫此之甚。

translations.literal: Moreover the south and west are not yet calm, arms and armor do not cease, and within the capital suburbs a great drought spans the seasons; the people are weary and things are withered — nothing exceeds this.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the south and west are not yet pacified, and war does not cease. Within the capital suburbs a great drought has persisted across seasons, and the people are weary and all things withered — the suffering has never been worse.

sentences.zh: 承天子育者，所宜矜恤。

translations.literal: One who bears Heaven's son and nurtures the people ought to show compassion.
translations.idiomatic: One who bears the Mandate of Heaven and nurtures the people ought to show them compassion.

sentences.zh: 伏願陛下追殷二宗感變之意，側躬聳誠，惟新聖道，節夜飲之忻，強朝御之膳，養方富之年，保金玉之性，則魏祚可以永隆，皇壽等於山岳。」

translations.literal: Your servant bows and wishes Your Majesty to follow the intent of the two Zong rulers of Yin in responding to change, bend the body and raise sincerity, renew the sage's way, moderate the pleasure of nightly drinking, strengthen the morning meal at court, nurture the years of growing strength, preserve the nature of gold and jade — then Wei's fortune can be forever exalted and the imperial longevity equal the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant bows and prays that Your Majesty will follow the example of the two sage kings of Yin, who responded to omens with humility and sincerity. Bend your person in earnest self-examination, renew the sage's way of governance, moderate the pleasures of nightly feasting, strengthen your morning meals at court, nurture your years of growing strength, and preserve the precious nature of your body — then the fortune of Wei may endure forever and Your Majesty's life span the mountains."

sentences.zh: 四年秋，除中書令，進號鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fourth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and advanced in title to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year he was appointed Director of the Secretariat and given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 永平元年秋，將刑元愉妾李氏，羣官無敢言者。

translations.literal: In autumn of the first year of Yongping, when Yuan Yu's concubine Lady Li was about to be executed, none among the officials dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the first year of Yongping, when Yuan Yu's concubine Lady Li was about to be executed, not one among the officials dared to speak up.

sentences.zh: 敕光為詔，光逡巡不作，奏曰：「伏聞當刑元愉妾李，加之屠割。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guang to draft the decree; Guang hesitated and did not compose it, memorializing: "Your servant has heard that Yuan Yu's concubine Li is to be punished with butchering execution.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Guang to draft the execution decree, but Guang hesitated and refused to write it. Instead he memorialized: "Your servant has heard that Yuan Yu's concubine Li is to be punished with butchering execution.

sentences.zh: 妖惑扇亂，誠合此罪。

translations.literal: Having bewitched and incited disorder, she truly deserves this crime.
translations.idiomatic: For having bewitched and incited disorder, she truly deserves punishment.

sentences.zh: 但外人竊云李今懷姙，例待分產。

translations.literal: But outsiders whisper that Li is now pregnant, and by precedent should await childbirth.
translations.idiomatic: But outsiders whisper that Lady Li is now pregnant, and by precedent a pregnant woman should be spared until she has given birth.

sentences.zh: 且臣尋諸舊典，兼推近事，戮至刳胎，謂之虐刑，桀紂之主，乃行斯事。

translations.literal: Moreover your servant has searched the old statutes and weighed recent affairs: execution extending to disemboweling the fetus is called cruel punishment — only rulers like Jie and Zhou practiced such things.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, your servant has searched the old statutes and weighed recent precedents. Execution that extends to cutting open a pregnant woman's womb is called cruel punishment — only tyrants like Jie and Zhou practiced such things.

sentences.zh: 君舉必書，義無隱昧，酷而乖法，何以示後？

translations.literal: The ruler's every act must be recorded; in principle nothing is concealed — cruelty that violates the law, how can it be shown to posterity?
translations.idiomatic: Every act of the ruler is recorded in history, and nothing may be concealed. How can cruelty that violates the law be shown to posterity?

sentences.zh: 陛下春秋已長，未有儲體，皇子襁褓，至有夭失。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's years are already advanced, yet there is no heir established; imperial sons in swaddling clothes have even met untimely death.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reached mature years, yet no heir has been established, and imperial sons still in swaddling clothes have met untimely death.

sentences.zh: 臣之愚識，知無不言，乞停李獄，以俟育孕。

translations.literal: Your servant's foolish understanding knows no withholding of speech; I beg to suspend Lady Li's case and await her delivery.
translations.idiomatic: In your servant's humble judgment, I know I must speak without reserve: I beg that Lady Li's case be suspended until she has given birth.

sentences.zh: 」世宗納之。

translations.literal: " The Shizong Emperor accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Shizong accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 延昌元年春，遷中書監，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Yanzhang he was transferred to Supervisor of the Secretariat, retaining his post as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Yanzhang he was promoted to Supervisor of the Secretariat while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 二年，世宗幸東宮，召光與黃門甄琛、廣陽王淵等，並賜坐，詔光曰：「卿是朕西臺大臣，今當為太子師傅。

translations.literal: In the second year the Shizong Emperor visited the Eastern Palace, summoned Guang together with Yellow Gate Attendant Zhen Chen, Prince of Guangyang Yuan Yuan, and others, all granted seats, and addressed Guang: "You are my great minister of the Western Terrace; now you shall be the Crown Prince's tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Emperor Shizong visited the Eastern Palace and summoned Guang, together with Yellow Gate Attendant Zhen Chen, Prince of Guangyang Yuan Yuan, and others, granting them all seats. He addressed Guang: "You are a great minister of my Western Terrace. You shall now serve as tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 」光起拜固辭，詔不許。

translations.literal: " Guang rose, bowed, and firmly declined; the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang rose, bowed, and firmly declined, but the edict would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 即命肅宗出，從者十餘人，敕以光為傅之意，令肅宗拜光。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Suzong to come out, with a dozen or so attendants, instructed him of the intent that Guang was to be his tutor, and commanded Suzong to bow to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Suzong to come forth with a dozen or so attendants, explained that Guang was to be his tutor, and commanded Suzong to bow to Guang.

sentences.zh: 光又拜辭，不當受太子拜，復不蒙許，肅宗遂南面再拜。

translations.literal: Guang again bowed and declined, saying he ought not receive the Crown Prince's bow; again he was not permitted, and Suzong thereupon bowed twice facing south.
translations.idiomatic: Guang again bowed and declined, protesting that he ought not receive the Crown Prince's bow, but again the emperor would not permit it. Suzong thereupon bowed twice facing south.

sentences.zh: 詹事王顯啟請從太子拜，於是宮臣畢拜，光北面立，不敢答拜，唯西面拜謝而出。

translations.literal: Household Steward Wang Xian petitioned to follow the Crown Prince in bowing; thereupon all palace officials bowed together. Guang stood facing north, dared not return the bow, and only bowed westward in thanks before departing.
translations.idiomatic: Household Steward Wang Xian petitioned to join the Crown Prince in bowing, whereupon all palace officials bowed together. Guang stood facing north, dared not return the bow, and only bowed westward in thanks before departing.

sentences.zh: 於是賜光繡綵一百匹，琛、淵等各有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon Guang was granted one hundred bolts of embroidered silk; Chen, Yuan, and the others each received gifts in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was then granted one hundred bolts of embroidered silk, while Chen, Yuan, and the others each received gifts in proportion.

sentences.zh: 尋授太子少傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon formally appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷右光祿大夫，侍中、監如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness while retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，世宗夜崩。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Shizong Emperor died suddenly at night.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year Emperor Shizong died suddenly in the night.

sentences.zh: 光與侍中、領軍將軍于忠迎肅宗於東宮，安撫內外，光有力焉。

translations.literal: Guang together with Palace Attendant and Commandant-in-Chief Yu Zhong welcomed Suzong from the Eastern Palace and pacified inner and outer circles; Guang had a strong hand in it.
translations.idiomatic: Guang, together with Palace Attendant and Commandant-in-Chief Yu Zhong, brought Suzong from the Eastern Palace and pacified the court and realm. Guang played a decisive role in the transition.

sentences.zh: 帝崩後二日，廣平王懷扶疾入臨，以母弟之親，徑至太極西廡，哀慟禁內，呼侍中、黃門、領軍、二衞，云身欲上殿哭大行，又須入見主上。

translations.literal: Two days after the emperor's death, Prince of Guangping Huai, supporting himself in illness, entered to mourn; by virtue of kinship as younger brother of the same mother, he went straight to the western gallery of Taiji, wailing in grief within the forbidden precincts, and called to the Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate, Commandant-in-Chief, and the Two Guards, saying he wished to ascend the hall to mourn the late emperor and also needed to enter and see the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after the emperor's death, Prince of Guangping Huai, though ill, came to mourn. As younger brother of the same mother as the late emperor, he went straight to the western gallery of the Taiji Hall and wailed within the forbidden precincts. He summoned the Palace Attendant, Yellow Gate officials, Commandant-in-Chief, and the Two Guards, declaring that he wished to ascend the hall to mourn the late emperor and also needed an audience with the new sovereign.

sentences.zh: 諸人皆愕然相視，無敢抗對者。

translations.literal: All looked at one another in astonishment, and none dared to resist.
translations.idiomatic: All looked at one another in astonishment, and none dared to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 光獨攘衰振杖，引漢光武初崩，太尉趙憙橫劍當階，推下親王故事，辭色甚厲，聞者莫不稱善，壯光理義有據。

translations.literal: Guang alone seized his mourning garment and shook his staff, citing the precedent when Emperor Guangwu of Han first died and Grand Commandant Zhao Xi barred the steps with his sword and pushed down the imperial princes; his words and bearing were very stern, and all who heard praised him, admiring that Guang's reasoning was well grounded.
translations.idiomatic: Guang alone seized his mourning garment and shook his staff. Citing the precedent of Grand Commandant Zhao Xi, who barred the palace steps with his sword when Emperor Guangwu first died and forced the imperial princes back, Guang spoke with fierce severity. All who heard him praised his conduct and admired the solid ground of his reasoning.

sentences.zh: 懷聲淚俱止，云侍中以古事裁我，我不敢不服。

translations.literal: Huai's voice and tears both stopped; he said, "The Palace Attendant judges me by ancient affairs — I dare not disobey."
translations.idiomatic: Huai's voice and tears alike fell silent. He said, "The Palace Attendant judges me by the precedents of antiquity — I dare not disobey."

sentences.zh: 於是遂還，頻遣左右致謝。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew, repeatedly sending his attendants to express thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon withdrew, repeatedly sending his attendants to express his thanks.

sentences.zh: 初，永平四年，以黃門郎孫惠蔚代光領著作，惠蔚首尾五載，無所厝意。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the fourth year of Yongping, Yellow Gate Gentleman Sun Huiwei was appointed in Guang's place to head the Writing Office; from beginning to end for five years he applied no effort.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the fourth year of Yongping, Yellow Gate Gentleman Sun Huiwei had been appointed to replace Guang as head of the Writing Office. For five years Sun had applied no effort to the task.

sentences.zh: 至是三月，尚書令、任城王澄表光宜還史任，於是詔光還領著作。

translations.literal: At this time in the third month, Minister of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng memorialized that Guang ought to return to the historiographical post; thereupon an edict ordered Guang to resume heading the Writing Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of this year, Minister of the Masters of Writing and Prince of Rencheng Yuan Cheng memorialized that Guang ought to resume his historiographical duties. An edict thereupon ordered Guang to head the Writing Office once again.

sentences.zh: 四月，遷特進。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was transferred to Special Advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was promoted to Special Advance.

sentences.zh: 五月，以奉迎肅宗之功，封光博平縣開國公，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, for his achievement in welcoming Suzong, Guang was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Boping county with a fief of two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, for his achievement in welcoming Suzong to the throne, Guang was enfeoffed as Duke of Boping with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 七月，領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he concurrently served as Libationer of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was appointed Libationer of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔光乘步挽於雲龍門出入。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict ordered that Guang ride in a hand-drawn carriage when entering and leaving through the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict granted Guang the privilege of riding in a hand-drawn carriage when entering and leaving through the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 尋遷車騎大將軍、儀同三司。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry with ceremonial parity to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 靈太后臨朝之後，光累表遜位。

translations.literal: After Empress Dowager Ling assumed the regency, Guang repeatedly memorialized to yield his position.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Ling assumed the regency, Guang repeatedly petitioned to resign his offices.

sentences.zh: 于忠擅權，光依附之。

translations.literal: Yu Zhong monopolized power, and Guang attached himself to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Zhong monopolized power, Guang aligned himself with him.

sentences.zh: 及忠稍被疏黜，光并送章綬冠服茅土，表至十餘上。

translations.literal: When Zhong was gradually distanced and dismissed, Guang also sent back his seals, cords, cap, robes, and fief lands, submitting more than ten memorials.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong was gradually distanced and dismissed, Guang likewise returned his seals, cords, cap, robes, and fief lands, submitting more than ten petitions to that effect.

sentences.zh: 靈太后優答不許。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ling graciously replied but did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling responded graciously but would not permit his resignation.

sentences.zh: 有司奏追于忠及光封邑。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized to recover the fiefs of Yu Zhong and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices petitioned to recover the fiefs granted to Yu Zhong and Guang.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年二月，太師、高陽王雍等奏舉光授肅宗經。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Xiping, Grand Preceptor and Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong and others memorialized recommending Guang to instruct Suzong in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Xiping, Grand Preceptor and Prince of Gaoyang Yuan Yong and others recommended Guang to instruct Emperor Suzong in the classics.

sentences.zh: 初，光有德於靈太后，語在于忠傳。

translations.literal: Earlier, Guang had shown kindness to Empress Dowager Ling; the account is given in the biography of Yu Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Guang had rendered a service to Empress Dowager Ling; the full account is given in the biography of Yu Zhong.

sentences.zh: 四月，更封光平恩縣開國侯，食邑一千戶，以朝陽伯轉授第二子勗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Guang was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of the State of Ping'en county with a fief of one thousand households; the title Marquis of Chaoyang was transferred to his second son Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Guang was re-enfeoffed as Marquis of Ping'en with a fief of one thousand households, and his former title Marquis of Chaoyang was transferred to his second son Xu.

sentences.zh: 其月，敕賜羊車一乘。

translations.literal: That same month an edict granted him one sheep-drawn carriage.
translations.idiomatic: That same month an edict granted him a sheep-drawn carriage.

sentences.zh: 時靈太后臨朝，每於後園親執弓矢，光乃表上中古婦人文章，因以致諫曰：「孔子云：『士志於道，據於德，依於仁，遊於藝。

translations.literal: At this time Empress Dowager Ling held court and personally took up bow and arrow in the rear garden; Guang thereupon memorialized presenting writings by women of middle antiquity, and thereby offered remonstrance, saying: "Confucius said: 'The gentleman sets his mind on the Way, takes his stand in virtue, relies on benevolence, and finds recreation in the arts.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Empress Dowager Ling held court and personally took up bow and arrow in the rear garden. Guang thereupon submitted a collection of writings by women of middle antiquity and offered remonstrance, saying, "Confucius said, 'The gentleman sets his mind on the Way, takes his stand in virtue, relies on benevolence, and finds recreation in the arts.

sentences.zh: 』藝謂禮、樂、書、數、射、御。

translations.literal: ' The arts mean ritual, music, writing, calculation, archery, and charioteering.
translations.idiomatic: ' The arts mean ritual, music, writing, calculation, archery, and charioteering.

sentences.zh: 明前四業，丈夫婦人所同修者。

translations.literal: The first four pursuits are clearly what men and women alike should cultivate together.
translations.idiomatic: The first four pursuits are clearly what men and women alike should cultivate together.

sentences.zh: 若射、御，唯主男子事，不及女。

translations.literal: As for archery and charioteering, these are solely men's affairs and do not extend to women.
translations.idiomatic: Archery and charioteering, however, are solely men's affairs and do not extend to women.

sentences.zh: 古之賢妃烈媛，母儀家國，垂訓四海，宣教九宗，可秉道懷德，[1]率遵仁禮。

translations.literal: The worthy consorts and heroic ladies of antiquity were models for family and state, left teachings to the four seas, spread instruction to the nine clans — they could uphold the Way and embrace virtue, leading all to follow benevolence and ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy consorts and heroic ladies of antiquity served as models for family and state, left teachings to the four seas, and spread instruction to the nine clans. They upheld the Way and embraced virtue, leading all to follow benevolence and ritual.

sentences.zh: 是以漢后馬鄧，術邁祖考，羊嬪蔡氏，具體伯喈。

translations.literal: Thus the Han empresses Ma and Deng surpassed their forebears in learning, and Lady Yang of the Cai clan embodied the full stature of Cai Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Han empresses of the Ma and Deng clans surpassed their forebears in learning, and Lady Yang of the Cai clan embodied the full stature of Cai Yong.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇太后含聖履仁，臨朝闡化，肅雍愷悌，靖徽齊穆，孝祀通於神明，和風溢于區宇。

translations.literal: Your servant bows: the Empress Dowager embodies sageliness and treads in benevolence, holds court and spreads transformation, is dignified and harmonious, gentle and kindly, tranquil and splendid, uniformly reverent; filial sacrifices reach the spirits, and harmonious winds overflow the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant bows before the Empress Dowager, who embodies sagely wisdom and treads the path of benevolence, holds court and spreads civilization, and is dignified, harmonious, gentle, and kindly. Her filial sacrifices reach the spirits, and harmonious winds overflow the realm.

sentences.zh: 因時暇豫，清暑林園，遠藐姑射，眷言矍相，弦矢所發，必中正鵠，威靈遐暢，義震上下。

translations.literal: Taking leisure in season, cooling herself in the wooded garden, gazing far toward Mount Guye, turning her regard to Juexiang — wherever her bowstring and arrow flew, she must hit the target center; her majesty and spirit extended afar, her righteousness shaking above and below.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leisure in season, she cooled herself in the wooded garden, gazing far toward Mount Guye and turning her regard to Juexiang. Wherever her bowstring and arrow flew, she struck the target's center. Her majesty and spirit extended afar, and her righteousness inspired awe above and below.

sentences.zh: 文武懾心，左右悅目，吾王不遊，吾何以休，不窺重仞，安見富美。

translations.literal: Civil and military officials were awed in heart, attendants left and right delighted in eye — 'If our king does not tour, how shall we rest? If we do not gaze upon the lofty wall, how shall we see its splendor and beauty?'
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials were awed in heart, and attendants left and right delighted in what they saw — as the saying goes, 'If our king does not tour, how shall we rest? If we do not gaze upon the lofty wall, how shall we behold its splendor?'

sentences.zh: 天情沖謙，動容祗愧，以為舉非蠶織，事存無功，豈謂應乾順民，裁成輔相者哉。

translations.literal: Heaven's disposition is modest and humble; moved in bearing, she shows reverent shame, thinking that this activity is not silk-rearing and weaving, that the affair exists without achievement — how could this be called responding to Heaven and following the people, trimming and completing, assisting and complementing?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's disposition is modest and humble. Moved in bearing, Your Majesty shows reverent shame, thinking that archery is not silk-rearing or weaving and that the activity serves no useful purpose. How could this be called responding to Heaven, following the people, and assisting in the governance of the realm?

sentences.zh: 臣不勝慶幸，謹上婦人文章錄一帙，其集具在內，伏願以時披覽，仰裨未聞。

translations.literal: Your servant cannot contain his good fortune and respectfully presents one fascicle of the collected writings of women; the full collection is within. Your servant bows and wishes that you will peruse it in season, looking upward to supplement what has not been heard.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant cannot contain his joy and respectfully presents one fascicle of collected writings by women, with the full collection enclosed. Your servant bows and prays that Your Majesty will peruse it in due season, to broaden what has not yet been heard.

sentences.zh: 息彎挾之勞，納閑拱之泰，頤精養壽，栖神翰林。」

translations.literal: Cease the labor of bending the bow and drawing the string; accept the ease of leisure with folded hands; nourish essence and preserve longevity; let the spirit dwell in the forest of brushes."
translations.idiomatic: Lay aside the labor of bending the bow, accept the ease of tranquil repose, nourish your essence and preserve your longevity, and let your spirit dwell in the forest of letters."

sentences.zh: 是秋，靈太后頻幸王公第宅。

translations.literal: That autumn Empress Dowager Ling frequently visited the mansions of princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Empress Dowager Ling frequently visited the mansions of princes and dukes.

sentences.zh: 光表諫曰：「禮記云：『諸侯非問疾弔喪而入諸臣之家，是謂君臣為謔。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized in remonstrance: "The Book of Rites says: 'If a feudal lord enters his ministers' homes for any purpose other than inquiring after illness or mourning the dead, this is called ruler and subject making sport of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Guang memorialized in remonstrance: "The Book of Rites says, 'If a feudal lord enters his ministers' homes for any purpose other than inquiring after illness or mourning the dead, this is called ruler and subject making sport of one another.

sentences.zh: 』不言王后夫人，明無適臣家之義。

translations.literal: ' It does not speak of queen or consort, making clear that there is no propriety in going to ministers' homes.
translations.idiomatic: ' It does not speak of queen or consort, making clear that there is no propriety in a ruler visiting ministers' homes.

sentences.zh: 夫人父母在，有時歸寧，親沒，使卿大夫聘。

translations.literal: When a lady's parents are alive, she may at times return home for a visit; when they are gone, she sends a minister or grandee on a formal visit.
translations.idiomatic: When a lady's parents are alive, she may at times return home for a visit; when they have passed away, she sends a minister or grandee on a formal visit in her stead.

sentences.zh: 春秋紀陳、宋、齊之女並為周王后，無適本國之事。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals record that daughters of Chen, Song, and Qi all became queens of Zhou, with no account of going to their native states.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals record that daughters of Chen, Song, and Qi all became queens of Zhou, with no account of their visiting their native states.

sentences.zh: 是制深於士大夫，許嫁唁兄，又義不得；

translations.literal: This regulation is stricter for them than for scholar-officials; even to mourn a married brother is again not permitted by propriety;
translations.idiomatic: This regulation is stricter for them than for scholar-officials; even mourning a married brother is not permitted by propriety;

sentences.zh: 衞女思歸，以禮自抑。

translations.literal: the lady of Wei longed to return home and restrained herself by ritual.
translations.idiomatic: the lady of Wei longed to return home and restrained herself through ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 載馳、竹竿所為作也。

translations.literal: This is what 'Speeding the Carriage' and 'Bamboo Poles' were composed for.
translations.idiomatic: This is what the poems 'Speeding the Carriage' and 'Bamboo Poles' were composed to express.

sentences.zh: 漢上官皇后將廢昌邑，霍光，外祖也，親為宰輔，后猶御武帷以接羣臣，[2]示男女之別，國之大節。

translations.literal: When Han Empress Shangguan was about to depose the Marquis of Changyi, Huo Guang, her maternal grandfather, personally served as chief minister — yet the empress still sat behind a martial screen to receive the officials, showing the distinction between male and female, a great principle of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Empress Shangguan was about to depose the Marquis of Changyi, Huo Guang, her maternal grandfather, personally served as chief minister — yet the empress still sat behind a martial screen to receive officials, demonstrating the distinction between male and female, a great principle of state.

sentences.zh: 伯姬待姆，安就炎燎；

translations.literal: Bo Ji waited for her nurse and calmly accepted the blazing fire;
translations.idiomatic: Bo Ji waited for her nurse and calmly accepted the blazing fire;

sentences.zh: 樊姜俟命，忍赴洪流。

translations.literal: Lady Fan of Jiang awaited her orders and endured entering the torrent.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fan of Jiang awaited her orders and endured entering the torrent.

sentences.zh: 傳皆綴集，以垂來詠。

translations.literal: The chronicles all gathered these accounts to hand down to future praise.
translations.idiomatic: The chronicles gathered these accounts to hand down to future generations.

sentences.zh: 昨軒駕頻出，幸馮翊君、任城王第，雖漸中秋，餘熱尚蒸，衡蓋往還，聖躬煩倦。

translations.literal: Yesterday the imperial carriage went out frequently, visiting the mansions of Lord of Fengyi and Prince of Rencheng; though mid-autumn approaches, residual heat still steams, and with parasols going back and forth, the sacred person grows weary and fatigued.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday the imperial carriage went out repeatedly, visiting the mansions of Lord of Fengyi and Prince of Rencheng. Though mid-autumn approaches, the residual heat still steams, and with parasols going back and forth, Your Majesty's sacred person grows weary.

sentences.zh: 豐厨嘉醴，罄竭時羞，上壽弗限一觴，方丈甘踰百品，旦及日斜，接對不憇，非謂順時而遊，奉養有度。

translations.literal: Rich kitchens and fine wine, seasonal delicacies exhausted; toasts to longevity not limited to one cup, sweet dishes in a square foot exceeding a hundred kinds; from dawn until the sun slants, receiving and responding without rest — this cannot be called touring in accord with the season or nourishing with proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: Rich kitchens and fine wine, seasonal delicacies exhausted without limit; toasts to longevity not confined to a single cup; sweet dishes exceeding a hundred kinds. From dawn until the sun slants westward, receiving and responding without rest — this cannot be called touring in accord with the season or nourishing with proper measure.

sentences.zh: 縱雲輦崇涼，御筵安暢。

translations.literal: Even if the cloud carriage is lofty and cool and the imperial banquet comfortable and pleasant,
translations.idiomatic: Even if the cloud carriage is lofty and cool and the imperial banquet comfortable and pleasant,

sentences.zh: 左右僕侍，眾過千百，扶衞跋涉，袍鉀在身，蒙曝塵日，渙汗流離，致時飢渴，餐飯不贍，賃馬假乘，交費錢帛。

translations.literal: the attendants left and right number more than a thousand or hundred; supporting and guarding, trudging and wading, robes and armor on their bodies, exposed to sun and dust, sweat streaming and flowing, brought to hunger and thirst in season, meals insufficient, hiring horses and borrowing rides, exchanging fees in coins and silk.
translations.idiomatic: the attendants left and right number more than a thousand. Supporting and guarding Your Majesty, they trudge and wade with robes and armor on their bodies, exposed to sun and dust, sweat streaming down their faces, brought to hunger and thirst, their meals insufficient, hiring horses and borrowing rides at the cost of coins and silk.

sentences.zh: 昔人稱陛下甚樂，臣等至苦，或其事也。

translations.literal: Men of old said that when Your Majesty is greatly pleased, your servants suffer to the utmost — perhaps this is such a case.
translations.idiomatic: Men of old said that when the ruler is greatly pleased, his servants suffer to the utmost — perhaps this is such a case.

sentences.zh: [3]伏惟皇太后月靈炳曜，坤儀挺茂，誕育帝躬，維興魏道。

translations.literal: Your servant bows: the Empress Dowager's lunar spirit shines brilliantly, her earthly measure stands flourishing, she gave birth to the imperial person and upheld the rise of Wei's Way.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant bows before the Empress Dowager, whose lunar spirit shines brilliantly and whose earthly measure stands flourishing. She gave birth to the imperial person and upheld the rise of the Wei dynasty.

sentences.zh: 德踰文母，仁邁和憙。

translations.literal: Her virtue surpasses the mother of King Wen; her benevolence exceeds He Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Her virtue surpasses the mother of King Wen; her benevolence exceeds that of He Xi.

sentences.zh: 親以天至，遠異莫間；

translations.literal: Kinship reaches as heaven ordains, distant and different cannot come between;
translations.idiomatic: Kinship reaches as heaven ordains, and nothing distant or different can come between;

sentences.zh: 愛由真固，非俟虛隆。

translations.literal: love springs from genuine solidity, not awaiting empty elevation.
translations.idiomatic: love springs from genuine devotion, not from empty display.

sentences.zh: 紆屈鑾駕，降臨闉里，榮光帝京，士女藻悅。

translations.literal: Bending the imperial carriage, descending to the wards within the city gates, glory lights the imperial capital, gentlemen and ladies radiant with joy.
translations.idiomatic: Bending the imperial carriage to descend to the wards within the city gates brings glory to the imperial capital and fills gentlemen and ladies with radiant joy.

sentences.zh: 白首之耋，欣遇犧年；

translations.literal: White-haired elders rejoice to meet the years of Emperor Xi;
translations.idiomatic: White-haired elders rejoice to meet an age of peace like that of Emperor Xi;

sentences.zh: 青衿之童，慶屬唐日。

translations.literal: green-collared youths celebrate belonging to the days of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: green-collared youths celebrate belonging to an age as glorious as the Tang.

sentences.zh: 千載之所難，一朝之為易，非至明超古，忘驕釋吝，孰能若斯者哉？

translations.literal: What a thousand years finds difficult, made easy in a single morning — unless supremely enlightened, surpassing antiquity, forgetting pride and releasing stinginess, who could be like this?
translations.idiomatic: What a thousand years finds difficult, made easy in a single morning — unless one is supremely enlightened, surpassing antiquity, forgetting pride and releasing stinginess, who could accomplish such a thing?

sentences.zh: 魏元已來，莫正斯美，興居出入，自當坦然，豈同往嫌，曲有矯避。

translations.literal: Since the time of Emperor Yuan of Wei, none has rectified this beauty; coming and going, entering and leaving, should naturally be open and candid — how could it be like past suspicions, with twisted avoidance?
translations.idiomatic: Since the time of Emperor Yuan of Wei, none has matched this excellence. Coming and going should naturally be open and candid — how could it be like past suspicions, with twisted avoidance?

sentences.zh: 但帝族方衍，勳貴增遷，祗請遂多，將成彝式。

translations.literal: But the imperial clan is expanding, meritorious nobles increasing in rank; respectful invitations grow numerous and will become established custom.
translations.idiomatic: But the imperial clan is expanding and meritorious nobles are increasing in rank; respectful invitations grow numerous and will soon become established custom.

sentences.zh: 陛下遵酌前王，貽厥後矩，天下為公，億兆己任。

translations.literal: Your Majesty follows and weighs the former kings, bequeaths rules to posterity; the realm belongs to all, the hundred millions already entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty follows the example of former kings and bequeaths rules to posterity. The realm belongs to all, and the hundred millions are already entrusted to your care.

sentences.zh: 專薦郊廟，止決大政，輔養神和，簡息遊幸。

translations.literal: Devote yourself to offerings at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, decide only great affairs of state, nurture spirit and harmony, simplify and reduce touring.
translations.idiomatic: Devote yourself to offerings at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, decide only great affairs of state, nurture your spirit and harmony, and simplify and reduce your touring.

sentences.zh: 以德為車，以樂為御，考仁聖之風，習治國之道，則率土屬賴，含生仰悅矣。

translations.literal: Take virtue as your carriage and music as your driver; examine the wind of benevolence and sageliness, practice the Way of governing the state — then all within the four seas will rely on you, and living creatures will look up in joy.
translations.idiomatic: Take virtue as your carriage and music as your driver; examine the spirit of benevolence and sageliness and practice the Way of governing the state — then all within the four seas will rely on you, and all living creatures will look up in joy.

sentences.zh: 臣過荷恩榮，所知必盡，默默唯唯，愚竊未敢，輕陳狂瞽，分貽憲坐。」

translations.literal: Your servant excessively bears favor and glory; what he knows he must fully express. Silent and merely assenting — your servant's foolishness privately dared not lightly present wild and blind words, apportioning blame to the seat of law."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has excessively borne favor and glory and must express all he knows. Silent assent alone your servant's foolishness dared not offer; he ventures to present these reckless words, apportioning any blame to himself alone."

sentences.zh: 神龜元年夏，光表曰：「詩稱：『蔽芾甘棠，勿翦勿伐，邵伯所茇。

translations.literal: In summer of the first year of Shengui, Guang memorialized: "The Odes say: 'The spreading sweet pear tree — do not cut it, do not hew it; beneath it the Earl of Shao rested.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the first year of Shengui, Guang memorialized: "The Odes say, 'The spreading sweet pear tree — do not cut it, do not hew it; beneath it the Earl of Shao rested.

sentences.zh: 』又云：『雖無老成人，尚有典刑。

translations.literal: ' It also says: 'Though there is no elder of mature virtue, there are still the models and punishments.
translations.idiomatic: ' It also says, 'Though there is no elder of mature virtue, there are still the models and punishments of antiquity.

sentences.zh: 』傳曰：『思其人猶愛其樹，況用其道不恤其人。

translations.literal: ' The chronicles say: 'Thinking of the man, one still loves his tree; how much more when employing his Way not to care for the man?
translations.idiomatic: ' The chronicles say, 'Thinking of the man, one still loves his tree; how much more when employing his Way ought one to care for the man himself?

sentences.zh: 』是以書始稽古，易本山泉，[4]觀於天文，以察時變，觀於人文，以化成天下。

translations.literal: ' Therefore the Documents begin with examining antiquity, the Changes take their origin from mountains and springs; observing the patterns of heaven to examine seasonal change, observing the patterns of humanity to transform and complete the realm.
translations.idiomatic: ' Therefore the Documents begin with examining antiquity, and the Changes take their origin from mountains and springs. By observing the patterns of heaven one examines seasonal change; by observing the patterns of humanity one transforms and completes the realm.

sentences.zh: 孟子□實，[5]匡張訓說。

translations.literal: Mencius [text damaged], Kuang and Zhang instructed and explained.
translations.idiomatic: Mencius [text damaged in the manuscript], and the masters Kuang and Zhang instructed and explained.

sentences.zh: 安世記篋於汾南，伯山抱卷於河右。

translations.literal: Anshi recorded cases south of the Fen; Boshan embraced scrolls west of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi recorded cases south of the Fen River; Boshan embraced scrolls west of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 元始孤論，充漢帝之坐；

translations.literal: Yuanshi's solitary discourse filled the Han emperor's seat;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanshi's solitary discourse filled the Han emperor's hall;

sentences.zh: 孟皇片字，懸魏王之帳。

translations.literal: Meng Huang's fragmentary characters hung in the Wei king's tent.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Huang's fragmentary characters hung in the Wei king's tent.

sentences.zh: 前哲之寶重墳籍，珍愛分篆，猶若此之至也。

translations.literal: The sages of old treasured and valued tomb records and books, cherished and loved divided seal script — even to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: The sages of old treasured books and records and cherished ancient seal script — even to this degree.

sentences.zh: 矧迺聖典鴻經，炳勒金石，理為國楷，義成家範，迹實世模，事則人軌，千載之格言，百王之盛烈，而令焚荒汙毀，積榛棘而弗掃，為鼯鼬之所栖宿，童豎之所登踞者哉！

translations.literal: How much more the sacred classics and great scriptures, brilliantly carved on metal and stone, principles as the state's model, righteousness as the family's pattern, traces as the age's mold, affairs as humanity's track — sayings of a thousand years, splendid achievements of a hundred kings — yet now to let them be burned, desolate, defiled, and destroyed, heaped with brambles and thorns yet unswept, made the roost of flying squirrels and the perch of children!
translations.idiomatic: How much more the sacred classics and great scriptures, brilliantly carved on metal and stone — principles as the state's model, righteousness as the family's pattern, traces as the age's mold, affairs as humanity's standard, sayings of a thousand years, splendid achievements of a hundred kings — yet now to let them be burned, desolate, defiled, and destroyed, heaped with brambles yet unswept, made the roost of flying squirrels and the perch of children!

sentences.zh: 誠可為痛心疾首，拊膺扼腕。

translations.literal: Truly this can make one grieve to the heart and head, beat the breast and wring the wrists.
translations.idiomatic: Truly this can make one grieve to the heart, beat the breast, and wring the wrists in anguish.

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，孝敬日休，自天縱睿，垂心初學，儒業方熙。

translations.literal: Your servant bows: Emperor Your Majesty, filial reverence daily flourishing, naturally endowed with wisdom from Heaven, bends the mind to early learning, Confucian studies just now prospering.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant bows before the Emperor, whose filial reverence daily flourishes, who is naturally endowed with wisdom from Heaven, bends his mind to early learning, and under whom Confucian studies are just now prospering.

sentences.zh: 皇太后欽明慈淑，臨制統化，崇道重教，留神翰林。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager is reverent, bright, benevolent, and virtuous, holds court and unifies transformation, honors the Way and values teaching, keeps her mind on the forest of brushes.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager is reverent, bright, benevolent, and virtuous. She holds court and unifies civilization, honors the Way and values teaching, and keeps her mind on the forest of letters.

sentences.zh: 將披雲臺而問禮，拂麟閣以招賢。

translations.literal: About to open the Cloud Terrace to inquire into ritual, brush the Unicorn Pavilion to summon the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: She is about to open the Cloud Terrace to inquire into ritual and brush the Unicorn Pavilion to summon the worthy.

sentences.zh: 誠宜遠開闕里，清彼孔堂，而使近在城闉，面接宮廟，舊校為墟，子衿永替。

translations.literal: Truly one ought to open Que li from afar and cleanse that Hall of Confucius — yet instead it lies near within the city walls, facing the palace temples; the old school is a ruin, the green-collared students forever displaced.
translations.idiomatic: Truly one ought to open Que li from afar and restore the Hall of Confucius — yet instead it lies near within the city walls, facing the palace temples. The old school is a ruin, and the green-collared students are forever displaced.

sentences.zh: 豈所謂建國君民，教學為先，京邑翼翼，四方是則也？

translations.literal: Is this what is called establishing a state and ruling the people, with teaching as the first priority, the capital majestic, the four quarters taking it as their model?
translations.idiomatic: Is this what is meant by establishing a state and ruling the people with teaching as the first priority, the capital majestic, the four quarters taking it as their model?

sentences.zh: 尋石經之作，起自炎劉，繼以曹氏典論，初乃三百餘載，計末向二十紀矣。

translations.literal: Tracing the making of the stone classics, it began with the blazing Liu; followed by the Cao clan's canonical discussions — from the beginning some three hundred-odd years, counting to the end approaching twenty generations.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the making of the stone classics, they began with the Han dynasty of Liu; they were followed by the Cao clan's canonical discussions. From their beginning some three hundred years have passed, approaching twenty generations to the present.

sentences.zh: 昔來雖屢經戎亂，猶未大崩侵。

translations.literal: In times past, though they repeatedly suffered military disorder, they had not greatly collapsed or been invaded.
translations.idiomatic: In times past, though they repeatedly suffered military disorder, they had not greatly collapsed or been destroyed.

sentences.zh: 如聞往者刺史臨州，多構圖寺，道俗諸用，稍有發掘，基蹠泥灰，[6]或出於此。

translations.literal: As your servant has heard, in former times when regional inspectors governed provinces, they often built monasteries with images; monks and laymen in various uses slightly excavated, and foundation stones, treads, mud, and ash perhaps came from this.
translations.idiomatic: As your servant has heard, in former times when regional inspectors governed provinces, they often built monasteries with images. Monks and laymen in various undertakings slightly excavated the site, and foundation stones, treads, mud, and ash perhaps came from this.

sentences.zh: 皇都始遷，尚可補復，軍國務殷，遂不存檢。

translations.literal: When the imperial capital was first moved, repair was still possible, but military and state affairs were pressing, and so preservation and inspection were not undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial capital was first moved, repair was still possible, but military and state affairs were pressing, and preservation and inspection were not undertaken.

sentences.zh: 官私顯隱，漸加剝撤。

translations.literal: Official and private, open and hidden, gradually added stripping and removal.
translations.idiomatic: Official and private parties, openly and in secret, gradually stripped and removed stones.

sentences.zh: 播麥納菽，秋春相因，□生蒿杞，時致火燎，由是經石彌減，文字增缺。

translations.literal: Sowing wheat and planting beans, autumn and spring following one another, [text damaged] growing artemisia and wolfberry, at times causing fire — thereby the classic stones daily diminished and characters increasingly lacked.
translations.idiomatic: People sowed wheat and planted beans in succession through autumn and spring; [text damaged] artemisia and wolfberry grew, and fires broke out from time to time. Thereby the classic stones daily diminished and characters increasingly disappeared.

sentences.zh: 職忝冑教，參掌經訓，不能繕修頹墜，興復生業，倍深慚耻。

translations.literal: Your servant's office disgraces the heir's teaching, participates in managing the classics and instruction — unable to repair what is ruined and fallen, revive the living enterprise, doubly deep in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's office disgraces the heir's teaching and participates in managing the classics and instruction. Unable to repair what is ruined and fallen and revive this living enterprise, he feels doubly deep shame.

sentences.zh: 今求遣國子博士一人，堪任幹事者，專主周視，驅禁田牧，制其踐穢，料閱碑牒所失次第，量厥補綴。

translations.literal: Now your servant requests to send one Erudite of the Imperial University capable of practical affairs, solely in charge of touring inspection, driving off and forbidding pasturing in the fields, controlling trampling and defilement, calculating and reviewing the stone tablets' lost sequence, measuring and repairing what is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant now requests that one Erudite of the Imperial University capable of practical affairs be dispatched solely to tour and inspect the site, drive off pasturing, forbid trampling and defilement, calculate and review the stone tablets' lost sequence, and measure and repair what is missing.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「此乃學者之根源，不朽之永格，垂範將來，憲章之本，便可一依公表。

translations.literal: " An edict said: "This is the root source of scholars, the eternal standard of immortality, a model handed down to the future, the foundation of statutes and regulations — let all follow your memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict replied: "This is the root source of scholars, the eternal standard of immortality, a model for future generations, the foundation of statutes and regulations. Let all proceed according to your memorial.

sentences.zh: 」光乃令國子博士李郁與助教韓神固、劉燮等勘校石經，其殘缺者，計料石功，并字多少，欲補治之。

translations.literal: " Guang then ordered Imperial University Erudite Li Yu together with Assistant Instructors Han Shengu, Liu Xie, and others to collate the stone classics; where they were damaged or missing, he calculated the stone work and the number of characters, intending to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: " Guang then ordered Imperial University Erudite Li Yu, together with Assistant Instructors Han Shengu and Liu Xie, to collate the stone classics. Where stones were damaged or missing, he calculated the stonework and the number of characters, intending to repair them.

sentences.zh: 於後，靈太后廢，遂寢。

translations.literal: Afterward, when Empress Dowager Ling was deposed, the project was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, when Empress Dowager Ling was deposed, the project was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，靈太后幸永寧寺，躬登九層佛圖。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year Empress Dowager Ling visited Yongning Temple and personally ascended the nine-story Buddhist pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year Empress Dowager Ling visited Yongning Temple and personally ascended the nine-story Buddhist pagoda.

sentences.zh: 光表諫曰：「伏見親昇上級，佇蹕表剎之下，祗心圖構，誠為福善。

translations.literal: Guang memorialized in remonstrance: "Your servant has seen you personally ascend the upper levels, halting your carriage beneath the marked pagoda — reverent in heart toward the image-structure, truly for the sake of blessing and goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Guang memorialized in remonstrance: "Your servant has seen Your Majesty personally ascend the upper levels, halting beneath the marked pagoda — reverent in heart toward the sacred structure, truly for the sake of blessing and goodness.

sentences.zh: 聖躬玉趾，非所踐陟，臣庶恇惶，竊謂未可。

translations.literal: The sacred person and jade footsteps are not what should be trodden and climbed; officials and commoners are fearful and alarmed, privately thinking it not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sacred person and jade footsteps are not what should tread such heights. Officials and commoners are fearful and alarmed, and privately deem it inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 按禮記：『為人子者，不登高，不臨深。

translations.literal: According to the Book of Rites: 'As one who is a son of man, do not climb high, do not face the deep.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Book of Rites, 'As one who is a son of man, do not climb high, do not face the deep.

sentences.zh: 』古賢有言：策畫失於廟堂，大人蹷於中野。

translations.literal: ' The sages of old had a saying: plans go awry in the ancestral hall, the great man stumbles in the open field.
translations.idiomatic: ' The sages of old had a saying: plans go awry in the ancestral hall, and the great man stumbles in the open field.

sentences.zh: 漢書：上欲西馳下峻坂，爰盎攬轡停輿曰：『臣聞千金之子不垂堂，百金之子不倚衡，如有車敗馬驚，柰高廟太后何？

translations.literal: The Book of Han: the emperor wished to gallop west down a steep slope; Yuan Ang seized the reins and stopped the carriage, saying: 'Your servant has heard that the son of a thousand gold does not lean over the hall, the son of a hundred gold does not lean on the railing — if the carriage breaks or the horse is startled, what of the High Temple and the Empress Dowager?
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Han records that the emperor wished to gallop west down a steep slope. Yuan Ang seized the reins and stopped the carriage, saying, 'Your servant has heard that the son of a thousand gold does not lean over the hall, and the son of a hundred gold does not lean on the railing. If the carriage breaks or the horse is startled, what of the High Temple and the Empress Dowager?

sentences.zh: 』又云：上酎祭宗廟，出，欲御樓船。

translations.literal: ' It also says: when the emperor performed the autumn libation sacrifice at the ancestral temple and came out, he wished to ride a tower ship.
translations.idiomatic: ' It also records that when the emperor performed the autumn libation sacrifice at the ancestral temple and came out, he wished to ride a tower ship.

sentences.zh: [7]薛廣德免冠頓首，曰：『宜從橋，陛下不聽臣，臣以血汙車輪。

translations.literal: Xue Guangde removed his cap and knocked his head, saying: 'You ought to take the bridge; if Your Majesty will not heed your servant, your servant will stain the carriage wheels with his blood.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Guangde removed his cap and knocked his head on the ground, saying, 'You ought to take the bridge. If Your Majesty will not heed your servant, your servant will stain the carriage wheels with his blood.

sentences.zh: 』樂正子春，曾參弟子，亦稱至孝，固自謹慎，堂基不過一尺，猶有傷足之愧。

translations.literal: ' Music Master Zichun, a disciple of Zeng Shen, was also called supremely filial; though naturally cautious himself, with a hall foundation not exceeding one foot, he still had the shame of injuring his foot.
translations.idiomatic: ' Music Master Zichun, a disciple of Zeng Shen, was also called supremely filial. Though naturally cautious, with a hall foundation not exceeding one foot in height, he still felt shame for injuring his foot.

sentences.zh: 永寧累級，閣道回隘，以柔懦之寶體，乘至峻之重峭，萬一差跌，千悔何追？

translations.literal: Yongning's piled levels, its corridor paths winding and narrow — with a soft and delicate precious body, riding the utmost steep and heavy precipice — if by any chance you slip and fall, a thousand regrets cannot retrieve it?
translations.idiomatic: Yongning's piled levels and its winding, narrow corridor paths — with a soft and delicate precious body, mounting the utmost steep precipice — if by any chance you slip and fall, a thousand regrets cannot retrieve the loss?

sentences.zh: 禮，將祭宗廟，必散齋七日，致齋三日，然後入祀，神明可得而通。

translations.literal: By ritual, when about to sacrifice at the ancestral temple, one must observe dispersed fasting for seven days and concentrated fasting for three days, then enter to sacrifice — the spirits may thereby be reached and communicated with.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, when about to sacrifice at the ancestral temple, one must observe dispersed fasting for seven days and concentrated fasting for three days, then enter to sacrifice, so that the spirits may be reached.
