sentences.zh: 今雖容像未建，已為神明之宅。

translations.literal: Now though the image has not yet been erected, it is already the dwelling of the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Now though the image has not yet been erected, the structure is already the dwelling of the spirits.

sentences.zh: 方加雕繢，飾麗丹青，人心所祗，銳觀滋甚，登者既眾，異懷若面。

translations.literal: Carving and painting are being added, adorned with splendid cinnabar and green — what people's hearts revere, keen observation grows ever greater; those who ascend are already numerous, diverse thoughts as if face to face.
translations.idiomatic: Carving and painting are being added, adorned with splendid colors. What people's hearts revere draws ever keener observation. Those who ascend are already numerous, and diverse thoughts arise as if face to face.

sentences.zh: 縱一人之身恒盡誠潔，豈左右臣妾各竭虔仰？

translations.literal: Even if one person's body constantly fulfills sincerity and purity, can attendants left and right, male and female, each exhaust reverence and respect?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Your Majesty's person constantly fulfills sincerity and purity, can attendants left and right, male and female, each exhaust reverence and respect?

sentences.zh: [8]不可獨昇，必有扈侍，懼或忘慎，非飲酒茹葷而已。

translations.literal: One cannot ascend alone; there must be escorts and attendants — fearing that some may forget caution, and this is not merely a matter of drinking wine or eating meat.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot ascend alone; there must be escorts and attendants. Your servant fears that some may forget caution, and this is not merely a matter of drinking wine or eating meat.

sentences.zh: 昨風霾暴興，紅塵四塞，白日晝昏，特可驚畏。

translations.literal: Yesterday wind and haze arose violently, red dust blocked the four quarters, the white sun dim at midday — especially something to fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday wind and haze arose violently, red dust blocked the four quarters, and the white sun was dim at midday — especially something to fear and dread.

sentences.zh: 春秋，宋、衞、陳、鄭同日而災，伯姬待姆，致焚如之禍。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals: Song, Wei, Chen, and Zheng suffered disaster on the same day; Bo Ji waited for her nurse and brought on the calamity of being burned to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records that Song, Wei, Chen, and Zheng suffered disaster on the same day. Bo Ji waited for her nurse and brought on the calamity of being burned to ashes.

sentences.zh: 去皇興中，青州七級亦號崇壯，夜為上火所焚。

translations.literal: In the Huangxing era, Qing province's seven-story pagoda was also called lofty and grand; at night it was burned by fire from above.
translations.idiomatic: In the Huangxing era, Qing province's seven-story pagoda was also called lofty and grand, yet at night it was consumed by fire from above.

sentences.zh: 雖梓慎、裨竈之明，尚不能逆剋端兆。

translations.literal: Although Zi Shen and Pi Zao had brilliance, they still could not reverse or forestall the earliest portents.
translations.idiomatic: Even the brilliance of Zi Shen and Pi Zao could not reverse or forestall the earliest portents.

sentences.zh: 變起倉卒，預備不虞。

translations.literal: Calamity arises in haste; one must prepare against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Calamity arises in haste, and one must prepare against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 天道幽遠，自昔深誡。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven is obscure and distant; from ancient times there have been deep admonitions.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of Heaven is obscure and distant, and from ancient times there have been profound admonitions against presumption.

sentences.zh: 墟墓必哀，廟社致敬，望塋棲慟，入門聳慄，適墓不登隴，未有昇陟之事。

translations.literal: At ruins and tombs one must mourn; at temple and altar one pays respect; gazing at the burial mound one grieves in sorrow; entering the gate one shudders with awe; when visiting a tomb one does not ascend the mound — there is no practice of climbing and ascending.
translations.idiomatic: At ruins and tombs one must mourn; at temple and altar one pays respect. Gazing at a burial mound one grieves in sorrow; entering the gate one shudders with awe. When visiting a tomb one does not ascend the mound — there is no custom of climbing and ascending.

sentences.zh: 傳云：『公既視朔，遂登觀臺。

translations.literal: The Record says: "The Duke, having observed the new moon, then ascended the observation tower."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "The Duke, having observed the new moon, then ascended the observation tower."

sentences.zh: 』其下無天地先祖之神，故可得而乘也。

translations.literal: "Below it there are no spirits of Heaven, Earth, or the ancestors, therefore one may mount it."
translations.idiomatic: "Below it there are no spirits of Heaven, Earth, or the ancestors, and therefore one may ascend it."

sentences.zh: 內經，寶塔高華，堪室千萬，唯盛言香花禮拜，豈有登上之義。

translations.literal: In the inner scriptures, precious pagodas are lofty and splendid, with countless chambered niches; they only lavishly describe incense, flowers, and ritual prostration — how could there be meaning in ascending?
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist scriptures describe precious pagodas as lofty and splendid, with countless niches, and speak only of incense, flowers, and ritual prostration — where is the justification for climbing up?

sentences.zh: 獨稱三寶階，從上而下，人天交接，兩得相見，超世奇絕，莫可而擬。

translations.literal: Only the Three Treasures stairway is singled out, going from above downward; human and heavenly realms meet, both sides may see each other — transcendent and wondrous beyond compare, nothing can match it.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Three Treasures stairway is singled out for praise — it runs from above downward, linking human and heavenly realms so that both may be seen. It is transcendent and wondrous beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 恭敬拜跽，悉在下級。

translations.literal: Reverent prostration and kneeling — all are on the lower levels.
translations.idiomatic: Reverent prostration and kneeling all take place on the lower levels.

sentences.zh: 遠存矚眺，周見山河，因其所眄，增發嬉笑。

translations.literal: From afar one gazes and looks out, seeing all around the mountains and rivers; following what catches the eye, mirth and laughter increase.
translations.idiomatic: From afar one gazes and looks out over the mountains and rivers; whatever catches the eye provokes mirth and laughter.

sentences.zh: 未能級級加虔，步步崇慎，徒使京邑士女，公私湊集。

translations.literal: One cannot step by step increase devotion, pace by pace augment reverence; it only causes the gentlemen and ladies of the capital, public and private, to gather together.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot step by step increase devotion or pace by pace augment reverence. It only draws the gentlemen and ladies of the capital, public and private alike, to gather together.

sentences.zh: 上行下從，理勢以然，迄於無窮，豈長世競慕一登而可抑斷哉？

translations.literal: Those above go up, those below follow — reason and circumstance are such; this extends without end. How can one suppress and cut off for all generations the competition to climb once?
translations.idiomatic: Those above ascend and those below follow — such is the logic of the matter, and it extends without end. How can one suppress for all generations the competition to climb just once?

sentences.zh: 蓋心信為本，形敬乃末，重實輕根，靖實躁君，恭己正南面者，豈月乘峻極，旬御層階。

translations.literal: For heart-faith is the root and formal reverence the branch; to honor the branch and slight the root, to calm the branch and agitate the lord — one who with proper respect faces southward as ruler, would he monthly mount the lofty peak or every ten days climb the layered stairs?
translations.idiomatic: For faith of heart is the root and formal reverence the branch. To honor the branch while slighting the root, to calm the branch while agitating the sovereign — would one who with due respect faces south as ruler monthly mount the lofty peak or every ten days climb the layered stairs?

sentences.zh: 今經始既就，子來自勸，基構已興，雕絢漸起，紫山華臺，即其宮也。

translations.literal: Now the initial construction is complete, people come of themselves to encourage it; the foundation structure has risen, carving and ornament gradually arise — the Purple Mountain Flower Terrace is already its palace.
translations.idiomatic: Now the initial construction is complete and people come of their own accord to encourage it. The foundation structure has risen and carving and ornament gradually appear — the Purple Mountain Flower Terrace has already become its palace.

sentences.zh: 伏願息躬親之勞，廣風靡之化，因立制防，班之條限，以遏囂汙，永歸清寂。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes that Your Majesty cease personal toil, extend the transforming influence that sways all, then establish regulations and safeguards, promulgate them as statutes and limits, to check clamor and defilement and forever return to clarity and stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly wishes that Your Majesty cease the labor of personal attendance, extend the transforming influence that sways all, establish regulations and safeguards, and promulgate them as statutes and limits to check clamor and defilement and restore lasting clarity and stillness.

sentences.zh: 下竭肅穆之誠，上展瞻仰之敬，勿踐勿履，顯固億齡，融教闡悟，不其博歟。」

translations.literal: Below, exhaust sincerity of solemn reverence; above, display respectful veneration; do not tread or step upon it — thus firmly manifesting for endless ages; merging instruction and spreading enlightenment — is this not expansive?"
translations.idiomatic: Let those below exhaust their solemn reverence and those above display respectful veneration without treading or stepping upon it, firmly establishing this for endless ages. To merge instruction and spread enlightenment — is this not the greater path?"

sentences.zh: 九月，靈太后幸嵩高，光上表諫曰：「伏聞明後當親幸嵩高，往還累宿。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Empress Dowager Ling visited Mount Song. Guang submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant humbly hears that tomorrow Your Majesty will personally visit Mount Song, going and returning over many nights."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Empress Dowager Ling visited Mount Song. Guang submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Your servant humbly hears that tomorrow Your Majesty will personally visit Mount Song, with the journey there and back taking many nights."

sentences.zh: 鑾遊近甸，[9]存省民物，誠足為善。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage touring the near countryside, [9] inspecting and caring for the people and their livelihoods — truly sufficient as a good deed.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial tour of the nearby countryside, [9] to inspect and care for the people and their livelihoods, is truly a worthy act.

sentences.zh: 雖漸農隙，所獲栖畝，飢貧之家指為珠玉，遺秉滯穟，莫不寶惜。

translations.literal: Although it falls within the agricultural break, the harvest gathered ear by ear — hungry and poor households treat each as pearls and jade; leftover sheaves and fallen ears, none do not treasure and cherish.
translations.idiomatic: Although the journey falls within the agricultural break, the harvest gathered ear by ear is to hungry and poor households as pearls and jade. Leftover sheaves and fallen ears — none are not treasured and cherished.

sentences.zh: 步騎萬餘，來去經踐，駕輦雜遝，競騖交馳，縱加禁護，猶有侵耗，士女老幼，微足傷心。

translations.literal: Foot soldiers and cavalry over ten thousand, coming and going treading across the fields; chariots and imperial carriages mixed and crowded, competing and rushing crosswise — even with strict prohibition and protection, there is still damage and loss; gentlemen, ladies, old and young — enough to hurt the heart slightly.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand foot soldiers and cavalry come and go, treading across the fields. Chariots and imperial carriages mingle and crowd together, competing and rushing crosswise. Even with strict prohibition and protection, damage and loss still occur — enough to wound the hearts of gentlemen, ladies, old and young alike.

sentences.zh: 秋末久旱，塵壤委深，風霾一起，紅埃四塞。

translations.literal: At the end of autumn, drought has long persisted; dust and soil lie deep; when wind and haze arise together, red dust blocks the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of autumn drought has long persisted and dust lies deep on the ground. When wind and haze arise together, red dust blocks the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 轅關峭嶮，山路危狹，聖駕清道，當務萬安。

translations.literal: Yuan Pass is steep and perilous; mountain roads are dangerous and narrow; the sacred carriage clearing the way — utmost safety must be the priority.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Pass is steep and perilous and the mountain roads are dangerous and narrow. In clearing the way for the sacred carriage, utmost safety must be the priority.

sentences.zh: 乘履澗壑，蒙犯霜露，出入半旬，途越數百，飄曝彌日，仰虧和豫。

translations.literal: Riding and treading through ravines and gullies, exposed to frost and dew; going out and returning for half a ten-day period, the route spanning several hundred li; wind and sun exposure for full days — looking up, one's harmony and ease are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Riding and treading through ravines and gullies, exposed to frost and dew; going out and returning for half a month, with the route spanning several hundred li; enduring wind and sun for full days — this must impair Your Majesty's harmony and ease.

sentences.zh: 七廟上靈，容或未許；

translations.literal: The lofty spirits of the seven temples perhaps may not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: The lofty spirits of the seven temples perhaps may not permit it;

sentences.zh: 億兆下心，實用悚慄。

translations.literal: The hearts of the billions below truly tremble with fear.
translations.idiomatic: The hearts of the billions below truly tremble with fear.

sentences.zh: 且藏蟄節遠，昆蟲布列，蠉蠕之類，盈於川原，車馬輾蹈，必有殘殺。

translations.literal: Moreover, the season of hibernation is distant; insects spread abroad; wriggling creatures of every kind fill the streams and plains — chariots and horses trampling them must certainly cause slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the season of hibernation is still distant and insects spread across the land. Wriggling creatures of every kind fill the streams and plains, and chariots and horses trampling them must certainly cause slaughter.

sentences.zh: [10]慈矜好生，應垂未測，誠恐悠悠之議，將謂為福興罪。

translations.literal: [10] Compassion and cherishing of life should extend to the unforeseeable; your servant truly fears that idle public talk will say that blessing is being sought through sin.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Compassion and cherishing of life should extend even to the unforeseeable. Your servant truly fears that idle public talk will conclude that blessing is being sought through sin.

sentences.zh: 厮役困於負檐，爪牙窘於賃乘，供頓候迎，公私擾費。

translations.literal: Servants are exhausted by bearing loads on shoulder poles; guards and aides are distressed by hiring mounts; provisioning stations and escort receptions — public and private alike are disturbed and expended.
translations.idiomatic: Servants are exhausted by bearing loads on shoulder poles and guards and aides are distressed by hiring mounts. Provisioning stations and escort receptions disturb and drain both public and private resources.

sentences.zh: 厨兵幕士，方履敗穿，晝暄夜淒，罔所覆藉，監帥驅捶，泣呼相望。

translations.literal: Kitchen soldiers and tent guards, their square shoes worn through; warm by day, cold by night, with nothing to cover or pad them; overseers drive and beat them — weeping and calling out to one another.
translations.idiomatic: Kitchen soldiers and tent guards wear through their square shoes; warm by day and cold by night, they have nothing to cover or pad themselves. Overseers drive and beat them, and weeping and calling out reach from one to the next.

sentences.zh: 霜旱為災，所在不稔，飢饉荐臻，方成儉弊。

translations.literal: Frost and drought form disasters; everywhere the harvest fails; famine arrives repeatedly; frugality and hardship are just becoming the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Frost and drought have brought disaster; everywhere the harvest fails. Famine arrives repeatedly and frugality and hardship are just becoming the norm.

sentences.zh: 為民父母，所宜存恤，靖以撫之，猶懼離散，乃於收斂初辰，致此行舉，自近及遠，交興怨嗟。

translations.literal: As parents to the people, one ought to care for and comfort them; with calmness to soothe them, one still fears dispersal and separation — yet at the very start of harvest collection, this journey is undertaken; from near to far, complaints and sighs rise together.
translations.idiomatic: As parents to the people, one ought to care for and comfort them. Even when soothing them with calm governance one still fears dispersal and separation — yet at the very start of harvest, this journey is undertaken, arousing complaints and sighs from near and far alike.

sentences.zh: 伏願遠覽虞舜，恭己無為，近遵老易，不出戶牖。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly wishes that Your Majesty look far to Yu Shun, reverently restraining oneself in non-action; follow nearby the Laozi and Yijing, not going beyond the door and window.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly wishes that Your Majesty look far to Yu Shun, reverently restraining yourself in non-action, and follow nearby the Laozi and Book of Changes, not going beyond your door and window.

sentences.zh: 罷勞形之遊，息傷財之駕，動循典防，納諸軌儀，委司責成，寄之耳目。

translations.literal: Abolish travels that weary the body; cease journeys that harm the treasury; in action follow canonical safeguards; bring all within standard ritual; entrust to officials responsibility for completion; rely on them as one's eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: Abolish travels that weary the body and cease journeys that drain the treasury. Let your actions follow canonical safeguards and bring all within standard ritual; entrust responsibility to officials and rely on them as your eyes and ears.

sentences.zh: 人神幸甚，朝野抃悅。

translations.literal: Humans and spirits would be greatly blessed; court and countryside would clap for joy.
translations.idiomatic: Humans and spirits would be greatly blessed and court and countryside would rejoice.

sentences.zh: 」靈太后不從。

translations.literal: " Empress Dowager Ling did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling did not comply.

sentences.zh: 正光元年冬，賜光几杖、衣服。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Zhengguang, Guang was granted an armrest-cane set and clothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Zhengguang, Guang was granted an armrest and cane, and clothing.

sentences.zh: 二年春，肅宗親釋奠國學，光執經南面，百僚陪列。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year, Emperor Suzong personally performed the libation sacrifice at the National Academy; Guang held the classic facing south, and the hundred officials attended in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year, Emperor Suzong personally performed the libation sacrifice at the National Academy. Guang held the classic facing south while the hundred officials attended in ranks.

sentences.zh: 司徒、京兆王繼頻上表以位讓光。

translations.literal: The Minister of Education, the Prince of Jingzhao Ji, repeatedly submitted memorials offering his position to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Education, the Prince of Jingzhao Ji, repeatedly submitted memorials offering his position to Guang.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，以光為司徒、侍中、國子祭酒，領著作如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, Guang was appointed Minister of Education, Palace Attendant, and Chancellor of the National University, continuing as before in charge of the Compilation Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Guang was appointed Minister of Education, Palace Attendant, and Chancellor of the National University, while continuing as before in charge of the Compilation Office.

sentences.zh: 光表固辭歷年，終不肯受。

translations.literal: Guang submitted memorials firmly declining for years, and in the end refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted memorials firmly declining for years and in the end refused to accept.

sentences.zh: 八月，獲禿鶖鳥於宮內，詔以示光。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, a bald stork was captured within the palace; an edict was issued to show it to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, a bald stork was captured within the palace, and an edict was issued to show it to Guang.

sentences.zh: 光表曰：「蒙示十四日所得大鳥，此即詩所謂『有鶖在梁』，解云『禿鶖也』。

translations.literal: Guang submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has shown me the great bird obtained on the fourteenth — this is what the Odes call 'there is a tuan on the beam'; the commentary says 'the bald stork.'"
translations.idiomatic: Guang submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has shown me the great bird obtained on the fourteenth. This is what the Odes call 'there is a tuan on the beam'; the commentary says 'the bald stork.'"

sentences.zh: 貪惡之鳥，野澤所育，不應入殿庭。

translations.literal: A greedy and vile bird, bred in wild marshes — it ought not enter the hall and court.
translations.idiomatic: It is a greedy and vile bird, bred in wild marshes, and ought not enter the halls of the palace.

sentences.zh: 昔魏氏黃初中，有鵜鶘集于靈芝池，文帝下詔以曹恭公遠君子，近小人，博求賢俊，太尉華歆由此遜位而讓管寧者也。

translations.literal: Formerly in the Huangchu era of Wei, a pelican alighted at the Lingzhi Pool; Emperor Wen issued an edict citing how Duke Cao of Gong kept gentlemen at a distance and kept petty men close, and broadly sought the worthy and eminent — Grand Commandant Hua Xin thereby yielded his position and yielded to Guan Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly in the Huangchu era of Wei, a pelican alighted at the Lingzhi Pool. Emperor Wen issued an edict citing how Duke Cao of Gong kept gentlemen at a distance and petty men close, and broadly sought the worthy and eminent. Grand Commandant Hua Xin thereby yielded his position to Guan Ning.

sentences.zh: 臣聞野物入舍，古人以為不善，是以張臶惡𪀼，賈誼忌鵩。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that when wild creatures enter a dwelling, the ancients regarded it as ill omen; thus Zhang Jian hated the [owl], and Jia Yi dreaded the owl.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has heard that when wild creatures enter a dwelling, the ancients regarded it as an ill omen; thus Zhang Jian hated the [owl], and Jia Yi dreaded the owl.

sentences.zh: 鵜鶘暫集而去，前王猶為至誡，況今親入宮禁，為人所獲，方被畜養，晏然不以為懼。

translations.literal: The pelican merely alighted briefly and departed, yet the former king still took it as the utmost warning — how much more now, when it personally enters the palace precincts, is captured by men, and is presently being kept and raised, calmly without fear?
translations.idiomatic: The pelican merely alighted briefly and departed, yet the former emperor still took it as the utmost warning. How much more now, when this bird has personally entered the palace precincts, been captured, and is presently being kept and raised — all without alarm?

sentences.zh: 準諸往義，信有殊矣。

translations.literal: Measured against former precedents, the difference is truly great.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against former precedents, the difference is truly great.

sentences.zh: 且饕餮之禽，必資魚肉，菽麥稻粱，時或餐啄，一食之費，容過斤鎰。

translations.literal: Moreover, this gluttonous bird must rely on fish and meat; beans, wheat, rice, and millet — at times it also pecks and eats; the cost of a single meal may exceed a jin in weight.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, this gluttonous bird must be fed fish and meat, and at times it also pecks at beans, wheat, rice, and millet. The cost of a single meal may exceed a jin or more.

sentences.zh: 今春夏陽旱，穀糴稍貴，窮窘之家，時有菜色。

translations.literal: Now in spring and summer yang-drought persists; grain prices are slightly high; impoverished households at times show the color of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: Now spring and summer drought persists, grain prices are rising, and impoverished households at times show the color of starvation.

sentences.zh: 陛下為民父母，撫之如傷，豈可棄人養鳥，留意於醜形惡聲哉？

translations.literal: Your Majesty as parent to the people, cherishing them as one would a wound — how can you abandon people to feed birds and fix attention on an ugly form and vile cry?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, as parent to the people, cherishes them as one would a wound — how can you abandon people to feed birds and fix your attention on an ugly form and vile cry?

sentences.zh: 衞侯好鶴，曹伯愛雁，身死國滅，可為寒心。

translations.literal: The Marquis of Wei loved cranes; the Earl of Cao loved wild geese — body dead, state destroyed; enough to chill the heart.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Wei loved cranes and the Earl of Cao loved wild geese — both died and their states were destroyed. The example is enough to chill the heart.

sentences.zh: 陛下學通春秋，親覽前事，何得口詠其言，行違其道！

translations.literal: Your Majesty's learning penetrates the Spring and Autumn Annals; you have personally reviewed former affairs — how can you recite its words with your mouth yet act contrary to its Way!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's learning penetrates the Spring and Autumn Annals and you have personally reviewed former affairs — how can you recite its words yet act contrary to its Way!

sentences.zh: 誠願遠師殷宗，近法魏祖，修德延賢，消災集慶。

translations.literal: Your servant truly wishes that Your Majesty take as distant model the Yin founder, take as near law the Wei ancestor, cultivate virtue and extend welcome to the worthy, dispel disasters and gather blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant truly wishes that Your Majesty take as distant model the founder of Yin, take as near standard the Wei ancestor, cultivate virtue and welcome the worthy, dispel disasters and gather blessings.

sentences.zh: 放無用之物，委之川澤，取樂琴書，頤養神性。

translations.literal: Release useless creatures, commit them to streams and marshes; take pleasure in zither and books, nourish the spirit and nature.
translations.idiomatic: Release this useless creature to the streams and marshes; take pleasure in zither and books and nourish your spirit and nature.

sentences.zh: 」肅宗覽表大悅，即棄之池澤。

translations.literal: " Emperor Suzong read the memorial with great delight and immediately released it to a pool and marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong read the memorial with great delight and immediately released the bird to a pool and marsh.

sentences.zh: 詔召光與安豐王延明議定服章。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Guang and the Prince of Anfeng Yanming to discuss and fix ceremonial robes and insignia.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Guang and the Prince of Anfeng Yanming to discuss and fix ceremonial robes and insignia.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，詔光乘步挽至東西上閤。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, an edict ordered Guang to ride in a hand-drawn carriage to the Eastern and Western Upper Pavilions.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year, an edict ordered Guang to ride in a hand-drawn carriage to the Eastern and Western Upper Pavilions.

sentences.zh: 九月，進位太保，光又固辭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he was promoted to Grand Mentor; Guang again firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, he was promoted to Grand Mentor, but Guang again firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 光年耆多務，疾病稍增，而自強不已，常在著作，疾篤不歸。

translations.literal: Guang was advanced in years with many duties; his illness gradually increased, yet he forced himself unceasingly, constantly remaining at the Compilation Office; when critically ill he did not return home.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was advanced in years with many duties and his illness gradually worsened, yet he forced himself unceasingly and constantly remained at the Compilation Office. Even when critically ill he did not return home.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，肅宗親臨省疾，詔斷賓客，中使相望，為止聲樂，罷諸遊眺。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, Emperor Suzong personally visited to inquire after his illness; an edict cut off visitors; palace emissaries followed one after another; for his sake music was stopped and all excursions suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year, Emperor Suzong personally visited to inquire after his illness. An edict cut off visitors, palace emissaries followed one after another, music was stopped for his sake, and all excursions were suspended.

sentences.zh: 拜長子勵為齊州刺史。

translations.literal: His eldest son Li was appointed Governor of Qi province.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Li was appointed Governor of Qi province.

sentences.zh: 十一月，疾甚，敕子姪等曰：「諦聽吾言。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, his illness was severe; he instructed his sons and nephews, saying: "Listen carefully to my words."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, when his illness was severe, he instructed his sons and nephews, saying: "Listen carefully to my words."

sentences.zh: 聞曾子有云：人之將死，其言也善，啟予手，啟予足，而今而後，吾知免夫。

translations.literal: I have heard that Zengzi said: when a man is about to die, his words are good — 'Show me your hands, show me your feet; from now on I know I am spared.'"
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that Zengzi said: when a man is about to die, his words are good — 'Show me your hands, show me your feet; from now on I know I am spared.'"

sentences.zh: 吾荷先帝厚恩，位至於此，史功不成，歿有遺恨。

translations.literal: I have borne the former emperor's deep grace and risen to this position; the historical work is not completed — in death I have lingering regret.
translations.idiomatic: I have borne the former emperor's deep grace and risen to this position, yet the historical work is not completed — in death I have lingering regret.

sentences.zh: 汝等以吾之故，並得名位，勉之！

translations.literal: You, because of me, have all gained name and position — exert yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: You have all gained name and position because of me — exert yourselves!

sentences.zh: 勉之！

translations.literal: Exert yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourselves!

sentences.zh: 以死報國。

translations.literal: Repay the state with death.
translations.idiomatic: Repay the state with your lives.

sentences.zh: 修短命也，夫復何言。

translations.literal: Long or short life is fate — what more is there to say?
translations.idiomatic: Long or short life is fate — what more is there to say?

sentences.zh: 速可送我還宅。

translations.literal: Quickly, take me back to my residence.
translations.idiomatic: Quickly, take me back to my residence.

sentences.zh: 」氣力雖微，神明不亂。

translations.literal: " Although his breath and strength were faint, his spirit was not confused.
translations.idiomatic: Although his breath and strength were faint, his spirit was not confused.

sentences.zh: 至第而薨，年七十三。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his residence he passed away, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his residence he passed away, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞而悲泣，中使相尋，詔給東園溫明祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲、錢六十萬、布一千匹、蠟四百斤，大鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong heard and wept with grief; palace emissaries followed in succession; an edict granted the Eastern Garden warm-bright secret coffin, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, six hundred thousand coins, one thousand bolts of cloth, four hundred jin of wax; the Grand Herald supervised the funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong heard and wept with grief. Palace emissaries followed in succession, and an edict granted the Eastern Garden warm-bright secret coffin, one set of court robes, one suit of clothing, six hundred thousand coins, one thousand bolts of cloth, and four hundred jin of wax. The Grand Herald supervised the funeral rites.

sentences.zh: 車駕親臨，撫屍慟哭。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage came in person; he caressed the corpse and wept with anguish.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came in person, caressed the corpse, and wept with anguish.

sentences.zh: 御輦還宮，流涕於路，為減常膳，言則追傷。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage returned to the palace, shedding tears along the road; he reduced his regular meals; in speech he mourned and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to the palace, shedding tears along the road. He reduced his regular meals and spoke with mourning grief.

sentences.zh: 每至光坐講讀之處，未曾不改容悽悼。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to the place where Guang had sat lecturing and reading, he never failed to change expression and grieve sorrowfully.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to the place where Guang had sat lecturing and reading, he never failed to change expression and grieve sorrowfully.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，贈太傅、領尚書令、驃騎大將軍、開府、冀州刺史，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Establishment of Office, and Governor of Ji province, Palace Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, he was posthumously granted the titles of Grand Tutor, Concurrent Director of the Department of State Affairs, Grand General of Agile Cavalry with Establishment of Office, and Governor of Ji province, while retaining his post as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又敕加後部鼓吹、班劍，依太保、廣陽王故事，諡文宣公。

translations.literal: Further, an edict added rear guard music and ceremonial swords, following the precedent of the Grand Mentor and Prince of Guangyang; posthumous title Duke Wenxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Further, an edict added rear guard music and ceremonial swords, following the precedent of the Grand Mentor and Prince of Guangyang, and granted the posthumous title Duke Wenxuan.

sentences.zh: 肅宗祖喪建春門外，望轜哀感，儒者榮之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong attended the funeral procession outside the Jianchun Gate, gazing at the hearse with sorrowful feeling; Confucian scholars honored this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong attended the funeral procession outside the Jianchun Gate, gazing at the hearse with sorrowful feeling — an honor that Confucian scholars praised.

sentences.zh: 初，光太和中，依宮商角徵羽本音而為五韻詩，以贈李彪，彪為十二次詩以報光。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Taihe era, Guang composed pentatonic poems according to the fundamental tones gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu, and sent them to Li Biao; Biao composed twelve successive poems in reply to Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Taihe era, Guang composed pentatonic poems according to the fundamental tones gong, shang, jue, zhi, and yu and sent them to Li Biao. Biao composed twelve successive poems in reply.

sentences.zh: 光又為百三郡國詩以答之，國別為卷，為百三卷焉。

translations.literal: Guang furthermore composed poems for the hundred and three commanderies and states in reply; each state formed a separate fascicle, totaling one hundred and three fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Guang furthermore composed poems for the hundred and three commanderies and states in reply, with each state forming a separate fascicle — one hundred and three fascicles in all.

sentences.zh: 光寬和慈善，不逆於物，進退沉浮，自得而已。

translations.literal: Guang was broad-minded, harmonious, and charitable; he did not oppose things; advancing and retreating, rising and sinking — he was content in himself, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Guang was broad-minded, harmonious, and charitable. He did not oppose things, and in advancing and retreating, rising and sinking, he was content in himself — that was all.

sentences.zh: 常慕胡廣、黃瓊之為人，故為氣概者所不重。

translations.literal: He often admired the character of Hu Guang and Huang Qiong; therefore those of bold spirit did not esteem him highly.
translations.idiomatic: He often admired the character of Hu Guang and Huang Qiong, and therefore those of bold spirit did not esteem him highly.

sentences.zh: 始領軍于忠以光舊德，甚信重焉，每事籌決，光亦傾身事之。

translations.literal: At first the Director of the Attendants Yu Zhong, because of Guang's old virtue, trusted and esteemed him greatly; in every matter he consulted and decided, and Guang also devoted himself wholly to serving him.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Director of the Attendants Yu Zhong, because of Guang's old virtue, trusted and esteemed him greatly. In every matter Yu consulted and decided, and Guang also devoted himself wholly to serving him.

sentences.zh: 元叉於光亦深宗敬。

translations.literal: Yuan Cha also deeply revered Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Cha also deeply revered Guang.

sentences.zh: 及郭祚、裴植見殺，清河王懌遇禍，光隨時俛仰，竟不匡救，於是天下譏之。

translations.literal: When Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi were killed, and the Prince of Qinghe Yi met with disaster, Guang bent and nodded with the times and in the end did not rescue them — whereupon the realm mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Zuo and Pei Zhi were killed and the Prince of Qinghe Yi met with disaster, Guang bent with the times and in the end did not rescue them — whereupon the realm mocked him.

sentences.zh: 自從貴達，罕所申薦。

translations.literal: From the time he reached noble eminence, he rarely recommended others.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he reached noble eminence, he rarely recommended others.

sentences.zh: 曾啟其女壻彭城劉敬徽，云敬徽為荊州五隴戍主，女隨夫行，常慮寇抄，南北分張，乞為徐州長史、兼別駕，暫集京師。

translations.literal: Once he petitioned regarding his son-in-law Liu Jinghui of Pengcheng, saying Jinghui was garrison commander of Wulong in Jing province; his daughter followed her husband, constantly fearing bandit raids, north and south separated — requesting appointment as Chief Administrator of Xu province with concurrent Vice Governor, temporarily gathering in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Once he petitioned regarding his son-in-law Liu Jinghui of Pengcheng, saying that Jinghui was garrison commander of Wulong in Jing province, that his daughter followed her husband and constantly feared bandit raids with north and south separated — requesting appointment as Chief Administrator of Xu province with concurrent Vice Governor so they might temporarily gather in the capital.

sentences.zh: 肅宗許之。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong granted the request.

sentences.zh: 時人比之張禹。

translations.literal: People of the time compared him to Zhang Yu.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time compared him to Zhang Yu.

sentences.zh: 光初為黃門，則讓宋弁；

translations.literal: When Guang first served as Yellow Gate Attendant, he yielded to Song Bian;
translations.idiomatic: When Guang first served as Yellow Gate Attendant, he yielded to Song Bian;

sentences.zh: 為中書監，讓汝南王悅；

translations.literal: as Director of the Secretariat, he yielded to the Prince of Runan Yue;
translations.idiomatic: as Director of the Secretariat, he yielded to the Prince of Runan Yue;

sentences.zh: 為太常，讓劉芳；

translations.literal: as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, he yielded to Liu Fang;
translations.idiomatic: as Grand Minister of Ceremonies, he yielded to Liu Fang;

sentences.zh: 為少傅，讓元暉、穆紹、甄琛；

translations.literal: as Junior Tutor, he yielded to Yuan Hui, Mu Shao, and Zhen Chen;
translations.idiomatic: as Junior Tutor, he yielded to Yuan Hui, Mu Shao, and Zhen Chen;

sentences.zh: 為國子祭酒，讓清河王懌、任城王澄；

translations.literal: as Chancellor of the National University, he yielded to the Prince of Qinghe Yi and the Prince of Rencheng Cheng;
translations.idiomatic: as Chancellor of the National University, he yielded to the Prince of Qinghe Yi and the Prince of Rencheng Cheng;

sentences.zh: 為車騎、儀同，讓江陽王繼，又讓靈太后父胡國珍。

translations.literal: as Chariot-and-Horse General with Equal Honor, he yielded to the Prince of Jiangyang Ji, and again yielded to Empress Dowager Ling's father Hu Guozhen.
translations.idiomatic: as Chariot-and-Horse General with Equal Honor, he yielded to the Prince of Jiangyang Ji, and again yielded to Empress Dowager Ling's father Hu Guozhen.

sentences.zh: 皆顧望時情，議者以為矯飾。

translations.literal: All looked to the temper of the times; commentators regarded it as artificial display.
translations.idiomatic: All looked to the temper of the times, and commentators regarded this as artificial display.

sentences.zh: 崇信佛法，禮拜讀誦，老而逾甚，終日怡怡，未曾恚忿。

translations.literal: He deeply believed in the Buddhist dharma, performing prostrations and reciting scriptures; in old age this grew ever more intense; all day long he was serene and joyful, never angry or resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply believed in the Buddhist dharma, performing prostrations and reciting scriptures, and in old age this devotion grew ever more intense. All day long he was serene and joyful and never angry or resentful.

sentences.zh: 曾於門下省晝坐讀經，有鴿飛集膝前，遂入於懷，緣臂上肩，久之乃去。

translations.literal: Once, while sitting by day reading scriptures in the Secretariat, a dove flew and alighted before his knees, then entered his embrace, climbed along his arm to his shoulder, and after a long while departed.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while sitting by day reading scriptures in the Secretariat, a dove flew and alighted before his knees, then entered his embrace, climbed along his arm to his shoulder, and after a long while departed.

sentences.zh: 道俗贊詠詩頌者數十人。

translations.literal: Monks and laypeople who composed poems and hymns in praise numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of monks and laypeople composed poems and hymns in praise of this.

sentences.zh: 每為沙門朝貴請講維摩、十地經，聽者常數百人，即為二經義疏三十餘卷。

translations.literal: Whenever monks and court nobles invited him to lecture on the Vimalakirti Sutra and the Ten Grounds Sutra, listeners regularly numbered several hundred; he thereupon composed commentaries on the two sutras of more than thirty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever monks and court nobles invited him to lecture on the Vimalakirti Sutra and the Ten Grounds Sutra, listeners regularly numbered several hundred, and he composed commentaries on the two sutras totaling more than thirty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 識者知其疏略，以貴重為後坐

translations.literal: Those who understood knew his superficiality; because of rank and prestige he took the rear seat
translations.idiomatic: Those who knew his work recognized its superficiality; because of his rank and prestige, he took a seat in the rear

translations.literal: (doubtful)
translations.idiomatic: (doubtful)

sentences.zh: 於講次。

translations.literal: at lecture sessions.
translations.idiomatic: at his lecture sessions.

sentences.zh: 凡所為詩賦銘贊詠頌表啟數百篇，五十餘卷，別有集。

translations.literal: In all he composed several hundred pieces of poetry, fu, inscriptions, encomia, hymns, panegyrics, memorials, and letters, totaling more than fifty fascicles, gathered in a separate collection.
translations.idiomatic: In all he composed several hundred works of poetry, fu, inscriptions, encomia, hymns, panegyrics, memorials, and letters, totaling more than fifty fascicles, which were gathered in a separate collection.

sentences.zh: 光十一子，勵、勗、勔、勸、劼、勀、勍、劬、勩、勦、勉。

translations.literal: Guang had eleven sons: Li, Xu, Mian, Quan, Jie, Ke, Qiang, Qu, Yi, Jiao, and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Guang had eleven sons: Li, Xu, Mian, Quan, Jie, Ke, Qiang, Qu, Yi, Jiao, and Mian.

sentences.zh: 子挹，襲。

translations.literal: His son Yi inherited [the title].
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 武定末，太尉。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding, [he was] Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Wuding era, he served as Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 屬齊受禪，爵例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his title was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 挹弟損，儀同開府主簿。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Sun, Chief Clerk of an Equaling-the-Three-Dukes Opening-a-Grand-Ducal-Fief office.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Sun served as Chief Clerk of an office equal to the Three Dukes with a grand ducal fief.

sentences.zh: 勗，武定末，征虜將軍、安州刺史、朝陽伯。

translations.literal: Xu—at the end of Wuding, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Governor of An Province, and Marquis of Chaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu, at the end of the Wuding era, was General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Governor of An Province, and Marquis of Chaoyang.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, [his rank] was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 勔，字彥儒，亦有父風。

translations.literal: Mian, courtesy name Yanru, likewise had his father's character.
translations.idiomatic: Mian, courtesy name Yanru, likewise showed his father's character.

sentences.zh: 司空記室、通直散騎侍郎、寧遠將軍、清河太守，帶槃陽鎮將。

translations.literal: Secretary in the Minister of Works' office, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Unimpeded Service, General of Pacifying the Distance, Administrator of Qinghe, and concurrently Commander-in-Chief of Panpan Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Secretary in the Minister of Works' office, Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary on the Unimpeded Service, General of Pacifying the Distance, and Administrator of Qinghe, while concurrently commanding the Panpan garrison.

sentences.zh: 為逆賊崔景安所害。

translations.literal: He was killed by the rebel Cui Jing'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was killed by the rebel Cui Jing'an.

sentences.zh: 贈征虜將軍、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and appointed Governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 子權，太尉參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Quan, Aide to the Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His son Quan served as Aide to the Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 劼，武定中，中書郎。

translations.literal: Jie, in the Wuding era, was a Master of Writing in the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, during the Wuding era, served as Master of Writing in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 光弟敬友，本州治中。

translations.literal: Guang's younger brother Jingyou was Administrative Advisor for his home province.
translations.idiomatic: Guang's younger brother Jingyou served as Administrative Advisor for their home province.

sentences.zh: 頗有受納，御史案之，乃與守者俱逃。

translations.literal: He had quite a bit of taking bribes; when the censor investigated, he fled together with the jailers.
translations.idiomatic: He had taken quite a few bribes; when the censor investigated, he fled together with the jailers.

sentences.zh: 後除梁郡太守，會遭所生母憂，不拜。

translations.literal: Later appointed Administrator of Liang commandery, but when his birth mother died he declined the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Administrator of Liang commandery, but when his birth mother died he declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 敬友精心佛道，晝夜誦經。

translations.literal: Jingyou devoted himself heart and soul to Buddhism, reciting scriptures day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyou devoted himself wholeheartedly to Buddhism, reciting scriptures day and night.

sentences.zh: 免喪之後，遂菜食終世。

translations.literal: After his mourning period ended, he ate only vegetables for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning period ended, he ate only vegetables for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 恭寬接下，修身厲節。

translations.literal: He was respectful and generous in dealing with others, cultivating himself and steeling his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He was respectful and generous toward others, cultivating himself and steeling his integrity.

sentences.zh: 自景明已降，頻歲不登，飢寒請丐者，皆取足而去。

translations.literal: From Jingming onward, harvests failed year after year; those begging from hunger and cold all received enough and departed.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jingming era onward, harvests failed year after year; those begging from hunger and cold all received enough from him and went on their way.

sentences.zh: 又置逆旅於肅然山南大路之北，設食以供行者。

translations.literal: He also set up an inn north of the great road on the south side of Mount Suran, providing food for travelers.
translations.idiomatic: He also established an inn north of the great road on the south side of Mount Suran, providing food for travelers.

sentences.zh: 延昌三年二月卒，年五十九。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Yan Chang he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Yan Chang he died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 子鴻，字彥鸞。

translations.literal: His son Hong, courtesy name Yanluan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cui Hong, courtesy name Yanluan.

sentences.zh: 少好讀書，博綜經史。

translations.literal: From youth he loved reading and broadly mastered the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved reading and broadly mastered the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太和二十年，拜彭城王國左常侍。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Taihe, he was appointed Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Taihe, he was appointed Left Regular Attendant in the Kingdom of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 景明三年，遷員外郎、兼尚書虞曹郎中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingming, he was promoted to Supernumerary Master and concurrently Master in the Yu Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jingming, he was promoted to Supernumerary Master and concurrently served as Master in the Yu Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 敕撰起居注。

translations.literal: He was ordered to compile the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to compile the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，兼祠部郎，轉尚書都兵郎中。

translations.literal: Promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently Chief in the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau, then transferred to Master in the Armaments Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Chief in the Sacrificial Affairs Bureau, then transferred to Master in the Armaments Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 詔太師、彭城王勰以下公卿朝士儒學才明者三十人，議定律令於尚書上省，鴻與光俱在其中，時論榮之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered thirty grandees, court officials, and men of learning and talent from below the Grand Mentor, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, to discuss and establish statutes at the Upper Secretariat; Hong and Guang were both among them, and contemporary opinion regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered thirty grandees, court officials, and men of learning and talent from below the Grand Mentor, Prince of Pengcheng Xie, to discuss and establish statutes at the Upper Secretariat. Cui Hong and Cui Guang were both among them, and contemporary opinion regarded this as a great honor.

sentences.zh: 永平初，豫州城人白早生，殺刺史司馬悅，據懸瓠叛。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongping, Bai Zaosheng of Yuzhou city killed Governor Sima Yue and rebelled, holding Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongping, Bai Zaosheng of Yuzhou city killed Governor Sima Yue, seized Xuancheng, and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 詔鎮南將軍邢巒討之，以鴻為行臺鎮南長史。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered General Who Guards the South Xing Luan to attack him, appointing Hong Chief Clerk of the Southern Suppression Mobile Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered General Who Guards the South Xing Luan to attack him and appointed Cui Hong Chief Clerk of the Southern Suppression Mobile Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 徙三公郎中，加輕車將軍。

translations.literal: Transferred to Master in the Three Excellencies Bureau, with the additional title General of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Master in the Three Excellencies Bureau and given the additional title General of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 遷員外散騎常侍，領郎中。

translations.literal: Promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, concurrently serving as Master.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary while continuing to serve as Master.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年，將大考百僚，鴻以考令於體例不通，乃建議曰：「竊惟王者為官求才，使人以器，黜陟幽明，揚清激濁，故績效能官，才必稱位者朝昇夕進，年歲數遷，豈拘一階半級，閡以□僚等位者哉？

translations.literal: In the second year of Yan Chang, when a major evaluation of all officials was about to be held, Hong found the examination regulations structurally inconsistent and submitted a memorial saying: "I venture to consider that a king seeks talent to fill offices and assigns men according to their capacity, promoting the obscure and demoting the manifest, elevating the pure and discarding the turbid. Hence those whose merit matched their post and whose talent suited their rank could rise in the morning and advance by evening, moving up year by year—how could one be bound to half a rank and obstructed by [damaged text] colleagues of equal rank?"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yan Chang, when a major evaluation of all officials was about to be held, Cui Hong found the examination regulations structurally inconsistent and submitted a memorial saying: "I venture to consider that a king seeks talent to fill offices and assigns men according to their capacity, promoting the obscure and demoting the manifest, elevating the pure and discarding the turbid. Hence those whose merit matched their post and whose talent suited their rank could rise in the morning and advance by evening, moving up year after year—how could one be bound to half a rank and obstructed by [damaged text] colleagues of equal rank?"

sentences.zh: 二漢以降，太和以前，苟必官須此人，人稱此職，或超騰昇陟，數歲而至公卿，或長兼、試守稱允而遷進者，披卷則人人而是，舉目則朝貴皆然。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties down through before Taihe, whenever an office required a particular man and a man suited a particular post, some leaped upward in a few years to reach the Three Excellencies; some served long as acting officials or on probation, proved satisfactory, and advanced—open any record and every man was such; look at any court noble and all were the same.
translations.idiomatic: From the Two Han dynasties down through the period before Taihe, whenever an office required a particular man and a man suited a particular post, some leaped upward in a few years to reach the Three Excellencies, while others served long as acting officials or on probation, proved satisfactory, and advanced. Open any record and every man was such; look at any court noble and all were the same.

sentences.zh: 故能時收多士之譽，國號豐賢之美。

translations.literal: Thus the state could timely gather the praise of many scholars and was famed for the abundance of its worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the state could timely gather the praise of many scholars and was famed for the abundance of its worthy men.

sentences.zh: 竊見景明以來考格，三年成一考，一考轉一階。

translations.literal: I observe that since Jingming the examination rules require one examination every three years, and one examination advances one rank.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that since Jingming the examination rules require one evaluation every three years, and each evaluation advances one rank.

sentences.zh: 貴賤內外萬有餘人，自非犯罪，不問賢愚，莫不上中，才與不肖，比肩同轉。

translations.literal: More than ten thousand within and without, high and low—all who did not commit crimes, regardless of worth or foolishness, received middle or higher ratings; the capable and the incapable advanced side by side alike.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand officials within and without, high and low—all who had not committed crimes, regardless of worth or foolishness, received middle or higher ratings, and the capable and the incapable advanced side by side alike.

sentences.zh: 雖有善政如黃龔，儒學如王鄭，史才如班馬，文章如張蔡，得一分一寸必為常流所攀，選曹亦抑為一概，不曾甄別。

translations.literal: Even if one had good governance like Huang Gong, Confucian learning like Wang and Zheng, historiographical talent like Ban and Sima, or literary skill like Zhang and Cai, gaining one bit would be pulled back by the common run; the selection office likewise suppressed all to a single standard and never distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Even if one had good governance like Huang Gong, Confucian learning like Wang Su and Zheng Xuan, historiographical talent like Ban Gu and Sima Qian, or literary skill like Zhang Heng and Cai Yong, gaining even a little would be pulled back by the common run, and the selection office likewise suppressed all to a single standard without ever distinguishing merit.

sentences.zh: 琴瑟不調，改而更張，雖明旨已行，猶宜消息。

translations.literal: When lute and zither are out of tune, one must restretch them; though the bright decree has already been issued, it is still fitting to adjust and soften.
translations.idiomatic: When the lute and zither are out of tune, one must restretch them. Though the bright decree has already been issued, it is still fitting to adjust and soften it.

sentences.zh: 」世宗不從。

translations.literal: " Emperor Shizong did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Shizong did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 鴻弱冠便有著述之志，見晉魏前史皆成一家，無所措意。

translations.literal: At his capping Hong already had the ambition to write; seeing that the histories of Jin and Wei before him had each become distinct schools, he had no niche for his own effort.
translations.idiomatic: At his capping Cui Hong already had the ambition to write. Seeing that the histories of Jin and Wei before him had each become distinct schools, he found no niche for his own effort.

sentences.zh: 以劉淵、石勒、慕容儁、苻健、慕容垂、姚萇、慕容德、赫連屈孑、張軌、李雄、呂光、乞伏國仁、禿髮烏孤、李暠、沮渠蒙遜、馮跋等，並因世故，跨僭一方，各有國書，未有統一，鴻乃撰為十六國春秋，勒成百卷，因其舊記，時有增損褒貶焉。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Murong Jun, Fu Jian, Murong Chui, Yao Chang, Murong De, Helian Bobo, Zhang Gui, Li Xiong, Lü Guang, Qifu Guoren, Tufa Wugu, Li Gao, Juqu Mengxun, Feng Ba, and others—all because of the turmoil of the age usurped territory across regions, each had a national history, and none was unified. Hong thereupon compiled them as the Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms, completing one hundred fascicles, drawing on old records with additions, deletions, praise, and blame as occasion required.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Murong Jun, Fu Jian, Murong Chui, Yao Chang, Murong De, Helian Bobo, Zhang Gui, Li Xiong, Lü Guang, Qifu Guoren, Tufa Wugu, Li Gao, Juqu Mengxun, Feng Ba, and others—all because of the turmoil of the age usurped territory in separate regions, each maintained a national history, and none was unified. Cui Hong thereupon compiled them as the Spring and Autumn of the Sixteen Kingdoms, completing one hundred fascicles and drawing on old records with additions, deletions, praise, and blame as occasion required.

sentences.zh: 鴻二世仕江左，故不錄僭晉、劉、蕭之書。

translations.literal: Hong's family served the south for two generations, so he did not record the books of the usurping Jin, Liu, and Xiao [regimes].
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong's family had served the south for two generations, so he did not record the histories of the usurping Jin, Liu, and Xiao regimes.

sentences.zh: 又恐識者責之，未敢出行於外。

translations.literal: Fearing that the discerning would reproach him, he did not dare circulate it outside.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that the discerning would reproach him, he did not dare circulate it publicly.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞其撰錄，遣散騎常侍趙邕詔鴻曰：「聞卿撰定諸史，甚有條貫，便可隨成者送呈，朕當於機事之暇覽之。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong heard of his compilation and sent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Yong with an edict to Hong saying: "I hear that you have compiled and fixed various histories with excellent organization. You may submit whatever is completed, and I shall read it in the spare moments of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong heard of his compilation and sent Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary Zhao Yong with an edict to Cui Hong saying: "I hear that you have compiled and fixed various histories with excellent organization. You may submit whatever is completed, and I shall read it in the spare moments of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 」鴻以其書有與國初相涉，言多失體，且既未訖，迄不奏聞。

translations.literal: " Hong, because his book touched on matters connected with the founding of the dynasty and much of its language was improper, and because it was not yet finished, never submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Hong, because his book touched on matters connected with the founding of the dynasty and much of its language was improper, and because it was not yet finished, never submitted it.

sentences.zh: 鴻後典起居，乃妄載其表曰：

translations.literal: Later, when Hong oversaw the Veritable Records, he falsely included his memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Cui Hong oversaw the Veritable Records, he falsely included his memorial, which read:

sentences.zh: 臣聞帝王之興也，雖誕應圖籙，然必有驅除，蓋所以翦彼厭政，成此樂推。

translations.literal: I have heard that when emperors and kings rise, though they are born in response to portents and ordinations, there must first be elimination—this is how one cuts down despised government and achieves willing elevation.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when emperors and kings rise, though they are born in response to portents and ordinations, there must first be elimination—this is how one cuts down despised government and achieves willing elevation.

sentences.zh: 故戰國紛紜，年過十紀，而漢祖夷殄羣豪，開四百之業。

translations.literal: Thus the Warring States were chaotic for more than ten twelve-year cycles, yet the Han Founder exterminated the rival heroes and opened four hundred years of enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Warring States were chaotic for more than ten twelve-year cycles, yet the Han Founder exterminated the rival heroes and opened four hundred years of enterprise.

sentences.zh: 歷文景之懷柔蠻夏，世宗之奮揚威武，始得涼、朔同文，牂、越一軌。

translations.literal: Through Emperor Wen and Jing's gentle rule over barbarian and Chinese, and Emperor Wu's rising martial prowess, the Liang and Shu regions shared one script and the Zang and Yue regions followed one track.
translations.idiomatic: Through Emperor Wen and Jing's gentle rule over barbarian and Chinese peoples, and Emperor Wu's rising martial prowess, the Liang and Shu regions shared one script and the Zang and Yue regions followed one track.

sentences.zh: 於是談、遷感漢德之盛，痛諸史放絕，乃鈐括舊書，著成太史，所謂緝茲人事，光彼天時之義也。

translations.literal: Then Sima Tan and Sima Qian, moved by the Han's greatness and grieved that various histories had been abandoned, gathered old books and completed the Grand Historian's record—the meaning of "weaving human affairs to illuminate heavenly seasons."
translations.idiomatic: Then Sima Tan and Sima Qian, moved by the Han's greatness and grieved that various histories had been abandoned, gathered old books and completed the Grand Historian's record—the meaning of weaving human affairs to illuminate heavenly seasons.

sentences.zh: 昔晉惠不競，華戎亂起，三帝受制於姦臣，二皇晏駕於非所，五都蕭條，鞠為煨燼。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Hui of Jin was incapable; Chinese and barbarians rose in disorder; three emperors were controlled by treacherous ministers; two emperors died untimely deaths in improper places; the five capitals became desolate, reduced to ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Emperor Hui of Jin was incapable; Chinese and barbarians rose in disorder; three emperors were controlled by treacherous ministers; two emperors met untimely deaths in improper places; the five capitals became desolate and were reduced to ashes.

sentences.zh: 趙燕既為長蛇，遼海緬成殊域，窮兵銳進，以力相雄，中原無主，八十餘年。

translations.literal: Zhao and Yan became long serpents; the eastern sea receded into a distant realm; with desperate armies and sharp advances they contended by force; the Central Plain had no master for more than eighty years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao and Yan became long serpents; the eastern sea receded into a distant realm; with desperate armies and sharp advances they contended by force, and the Central Plain had no master for more than eighty years.

sentences.zh: 遺晉僻遠，勢略孤微，民殘兵革，靡所歸控。

translations.literal: The remnant Jin was remote and feeble in strategy; the people were ravaged by war and had nowhere to turn.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant Jin was remote and feeble in strategy; the people were ravaged by war and had nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 皇魏龍潛幽代，世篤公劉，內修德政，外抗諸偽，并冀之民，懷寶之士，襁負而至者日月相尋，雖邠岐之赴太王，謳歌之歸西伯，實可同年而語矣。

translations.literal: Our Wei dynasty lay hidden in dark Dai, generations devoted to Duke Liu; inwardly cultivating virtuous government, outwardly resisting the false states; people of Bing and Ji, men bearing talent, came carrying infants on their backs day after day in succession—even Bin and Qi's gathering to Grand King and the songs returning to the Western Overlord can truly be spoken of in the same breath.
translations.idiomatic: Our Wei dynasty lay hidden in dark Dai, generations devoted to Duke Liu; inwardly it cultivated virtuous government and outwardly resisted the false states. People of Bing and Ji and men bearing talent came carrying infants on their backs day after day in succession—even Bin and Qi's gathering to Grand King and the songs returning to the Western Overlord can truly be spoken of in the same breath.

sentences.zh: 太祖道武皇帝以神武之姿，接金行之運，應天順民，龍飛受命。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu, with divine martial bearing, received the Metal Phase's destiny, responding to Heaven and following the people, dragon-flying to receive the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Daowu, with divine martial bearing, received the Metal Phase's destiny, responding to Heaven and following the people, and rose like a dragon to receive the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 太宗必世重光，業隆玄默。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong restored radiance in the second generation; his enterprise rose in silent profundity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong restored radiance in the second generation, and his enterprise rose in silent profundity.

sentences.zh: 世祖雄才叡略，闡曜威靈，農戰兼修，掃清氛穢。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu, with heroic talent and keen strategy, spread his brilliant authority, combined farming and warfare, and swept clear the miasma.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu, with heroic talent and keen strategy, spread his brilliant authority, combined farming and warfare, and swept clear the miasma.

sentences.zh: 歲垂四紀，而寰宇一同。

translations.literal: Within nearly four decades, all under Heaven was unified.
translations.idiomatic: Within nearly four decades, all under Heaven was unified.

sentences.zh: 儋耳、文身之長，卉服、斷髮之酋，莫不請朔率職，重譯來庭。

translations.literal: Chiefs of Dan'er and tattooed lands, chieftains in plant-cloth and cut hair—all without exception requested the calendar and fulfilled duties, coming to court through double translation.
translations.idiomatic: Chiefs of Dan'er and tattooed lands, chieftains in plant-cloth and cut hair—all without exception requested the calendar, fulfilled their duties, and came to court through double translation.

sentences.zh: 隱愍鴻濟之澤，三樂擊壤之歌，百姓始得陶然蘇息，欣於堯舜之世。

translations.literal: Through hidden compassion and vast salvific bounty, the three joys and songs of pounding the earth—the common people at last could revive and rest content, rejoicing as in the age of Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Through hidden compassion and vast salvific bounty, with the three joys and songs of pounding the earth, the common people at last could revive and rest content, rejoicing as in the age of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 自晉永寧以後，雖所在稱兵，競自尊樹，而能建邦命氏成為戰國者，十有六家。

translations.literal: Since Yongning of Jin, though everywhere arms were raised and each strove to establish himself, those able to found states, take dynastic names, and become warring kingdoms numbered sixteen houses.
translations.idiomatic: Since Yongning of Jin, though everywhere arms were raised and each ruler strove to establish himself, those able to found states, take dynastic names, and become warring kingdoms numbered sixteen houses.

sentences.zh: 善惡興滅之形，用兵乖會之勢，亦足以垂之將來，昭明勸戒。

translations.literal: The forms of good and evil, rise and fall, the patterns of deploying forces and converging campaigns—these are enough to hand down to the future and make clear admonition and warning.
translations.idiomatic: The forms of good and evil, rise and fall, and the patterns of deploying forces and converging campaigns are enough to hand down to the future and make clear admonition and warning.

sentences.zh: 但諸史殘缺，體例不全，編錄紛謬，繁略失所，宜審正不同，定為一書。

translations.literal: But the various histories are damaged and incomplete, their structure not whole, compilation confused and errors in fullness and brevity—it is fitting to examine and correct discrepancies and fix them as one book.
translations.idiomatic: But the various histories are damaged and incomplete, their structure not whole, and their compilation confused with errors in fullness and brevity. It is fitting to examine and correct discrepancies and fix them as one book.

sentences.zh: 伏惟高祖以大聖應期，欽明御運，合德乾坤，同光日月，建格天之功，創不世之法，開鑿生民，惟新大造。

translations.literal: Your humble servant considers that Emperor Gaozu, in great sagacity meeting the age, reverently illumined and steering fate, matched the virtue of Heaven and Earth and shared the light of sun and moon, built merit reaching to Heaven, created laws without parallel, opened and carved for the living people a wholly renewed great creation.
translations.idiomatic: Your humble servant considers that Emperor Gaozu, in great sagacity meeting the age, reverently illumined and steered fate, matched the virtue of Heaven and Earth and shared the light of sun and moon, built merit reaching to Heaven, created laws without parallel, and opened and carved for the living people a wholly renewed great creation.

sentences.zh: 陛下以青陽繼統，叡武承天。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, with the green yang succession, wise martial bearing inherited Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, with the green yang succession, inherited Heaven with wise martial bearing.

sentences.zh: 應符屈己，則道高三、五；

translations.literal: Matching the signs and humbling oneself, then the Way surpasses the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;
translations.idiomatic: Matching the signs and humbling oneself, your Way surpasses the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors;

sentences.zh: 頤神至境，則洞彼玄宗。

translations.literal: Nourishing spirit to the ultimate realm, then penetrating that profound mystery.
translations.idiomatic: nourishing spirit to the ultimate realm, you penetrate that profound mystery.

sentences.zh: 剖判百家，斟酌六籍，遠邁石渠，美深白虎。

translations.literal: Discriminating among the hundred schools, weighing the Six Classics—far surpassing Shiqu, more splendid than Baihu.
translations.idiomatic: You discriminate among the hundred schools and weigh the Six Classics—far surpassing Shiqu and more splendid than Baihu.

sentences.zh: 至如導禮革俗之風，昭文變性之化，固以感彼禽魚，穆茲寒暑。

translations.literal: As for the wind of guiding ritual and reforming custom, the transformation of illuminating culture and changing nature—it truly moves birds and fish and brings harmony to cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: As for the wind of guiding ritual and reforming custom, the transformation of illuminating culture and changing nature—it truly moves birds and fish and brings harmony to cold and heat.

sentences.zh: 而況愚臣沐浴太和，懷音正始，而可不勉強難革之性，砥礪木石之心哉？

translations.literal: How much more so for a foolish minister bathed in great harmony, cherishing the Zhengshi tone—how could he not strive against hard-to-change nature and sharpen a heart like wood and stone?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for a foolish minister bathed in great harmony and cherishing the Zhengshi tone—how could he not strive against hard-to-change nature and sharpen a heart like wood and stone?

sentences.zh: 誠知敏謝允南，才非承祚，然國志、史考之美，竊亦輒所庶幾。

translations.literal: Truly I know my quickness falls short of Chen Shou of Runan, my talent short of Sima Biao—but the beauty of the Records of the States and historical investigations is what I privately aspire to.
translations.idiomatic: Truly I know my quickness falls short of Chen Shou of Runan and my talent falls short of Sima Biao, but the beauty of the Records of the States and historical investigations is what I privately aspire to.

sentences.zh: 始自景明之初，搜集諸國舊史，屬遷京甫爾，率多分散，求之公私，驅馳數歲。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Jingming I gathered old histories of the various states; just after the capital moved, most were scattered; seeking them in public and private, I traveled urgently for several years.
translations.idiomatic: From the beginning of Jingming I gathered old histories of the various states. Just after the capital moved, most were scattered, and seeking them in public and private collections, I traveled urgently for several years.

sentences.zh: 又臣家貧祿薄，唯任孤力，至於紙盡，書寫所資，每不周接，暨正始元年，寫乃向備。

translations.literal: Also my household is poor and salary thin; I rely solely on my own strength; as for paper running out and costs of writing, each time funds were insufficient—only by the first year of Zhengshi was copying nearly complete.
translations.idiomatic: Also my household is poor and my salary thin; I rely solely on my own strength. As for paper running out and the costs of writing, each time funds were insufficient, and only by the first year of Zhengshi was copying nearly complete.

sentences.zh: 謹於吏按之暇，草構此書。

translations.literal: Respectfully in spare moments from official duties, I drafted this book.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully, in spare moments from official duties, I drafted this book.

sentences.zh: 區分時事，各繫本錄；

translations.literal: Dividing affairs by period, each attached to its own record;
translations.idiomatic: I divided affairs by period, each attached to its own record;

sentences.zh: 破彼異同，凡為一體；

translations.literal: Breaking their discrepancies, making all one whole;
translations.idiomatic: broke their discrepancies and made all one whole;

sentences.zh: 約損煩文，補其不足。

translations.literal: Reducing redundant text, supplementing deficiencies.
translations.idiomatic: reduced redundant text and supplemented deficiencies.

sentences.zh: 三豕五門之類，一事異年之流，皆稽以長曆，考諸舊志，刪正差謬，定為實錄。

translations.literal: Cases like the three pigs and five gates, instances of one event in different years—all checked against the long calendar, verified against old chronicles, corrected for errors, fixed as true records.
translations.idiomatic: Cases like the three pigs and five gates, and instances of one event recorded in different years—all were checked against the long calendar, verified against old chronicles, corrected for errors, and fixed as true records.

sentences.zh: 商校大略，著春秋百篇。

translations.literal: After collation in outline, I composed one hundred chapters of Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: After collation in outline, I composed one hundred chapters of Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 至三年之末，草成九十五卷。

translations.literal: By the end of the third year, the draft reached ninety-five fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the third year, the draft reached ninety-five fascicles.

sentences.zh: 唯常璩所撰李雄父子據蜀時書，尋訪不獲，所以未及繕成，輟筆私求，七載于今。

translations.literal: Only the book by Chang Qu on Li Xiong father and son holding Shu I have searched for without finding; therefore I have not completed copying; I laid down my brush and sought privately—seven years until now.
translations.idiomatic: Only the book by Chang Qu on Li Xiong and his son holding Shu I have searched for without finding; therefore I have not completed copying. I laid down my brush and sought privately—seven years until now.

sentences.zh: 此書本江南撰錄，恐中國所無，非臣私力所能終得。

translations.literal: This book was originally compiled in Jiangnan; I fear it is not in China; it is not something my private strength can finally obtain.
translations.idiomatic: This book was originally compiled in Jiangnan, and I fear it is not available in China. It is not something my private strength can finally obtain.

sentences.zh: 其起兵僭號，事之始末，乃亦頗有，但不得此書，懼簡略不成。

translations.literal: Matters of raising troops and usurping titles, beginnings and ends—I have quite a bit, but without this book I fear brevity will leave it incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: I have quite a bit on the raising of troops and usurpation of titles, their beginnings and ends, but without this book I fear brevity will leave the account incomplete.

sentences.zh: 久思陳奏，乞敕緣邊求採，但愚賤無因，不敢輕輒。

translations.literal: Long I have wished to memorialize, begging an order to seek copies on the frontier, but being foolish and lowly I had no access and did not dare act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Long I have wished to memorialize and beg an order to seek copies on the frontier, but being foolish and lowly I had no access and did not dare act rashly.

sentences.zh: 散騎常侍、太常少卿、荊州大中正臣趙邕，忽宣明旨，敕臣送呈。

translations.literal: The Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Chief Rectifier of Jing Province, subject Zhao Yong, suddenly announced the bright decree ordering me to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Chief Rectifier of Jing Province, Zhao Yong, suddenly announced the bright decree ordering me to submit.

sentences.zh: 不悟九臯微志，乃得上聞，奉敕欣惶，慶懼兼至。

translations.literal: I did not expect that this humble wish of the nine marshes could reach the heights; receiving the decree I am joyful and fearful, gladness and dread together.
translations.idiomatic: I did not expect that this humble wish of the nine marshes could reach the heights. Receiving the decree, I am joyful and fearful, with gladness and dread together.

sentences.zh: 今謹以所訖者，附臣邕呈奏。

translations.literal: Now I respectfully submit what is completed, attached through Subject Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Now I respectfully submit what is completed, attached through Zhao Yong.

sentences.zh: 臣又別作序例一卷，年表一卷，仰表皇朝統括大義，俯明愚臣著錄微體。

translations.literal: I have also separately composed one fascicle of preface and principles and one fascicle of chronological table—looking up to express the grand theme unifying our dynasty, looking down to clarify the humble structure of my own compilation.
translations.idiomatic: I have also separately composed one fascicle of preface and principles and one fascicle of chronological table—looking up to express the grand theme unifying our dynasty and looking down to clarify the humble structure of my own compilation.

sentences.zh: 徒竊慕古人立言美意，文致疏鄙，無一可觀，簡御之日，伏深慚悸。

translations.literal: I merely stole admiration for the ancients' beautiful intent in setting words; my style is crude and vulgar, nothing worth viewing—on the day of your brief inspection I prostrate myself in deep shame and trepidation.
translations.idiomatic: I merely stole admiration for the ancients' beautiful intent in setting words. My style is crude and vulgar and nothing worth viewing. On the day of your brief inspection I prostrate myself in deep shame and trepidation.

sentences.zh: 鴻意如此，然自正光以前，不敢顯行其書。

translations.literal: Hong's intent was so, yet before Zhengguang he did not dare openly circulate his book.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong's intent was so, yet before Zhengguang he did not dare openly circulate his book.

sentences.zh: 自後以其伯光貴重當朝，知時人未能發明其事，乃頗相傳讀。

translations.literal: Afterward, because his elder uncle Guang was esteemed in the court, knowing people of the time could not expose the matter, copies were rather widely passed and read.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, because his elder uncle Cui Guang was esteemed at court, and knowing people of the time could not expose the matter, copies were rather widely passed around and read.

sentences.zh: 亦以光故，執事者遂不論之。

translations.literal: Also because of Guang, those in charge did not pursue the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Also because of Cui Guang, those in charge did not pursue the matter.

sentences.zh: 鴻經綜既廣，多有違謬：至如太祖天興二年，姚興改號，鴻以為改在元年；

translations.literal: Hong's synthesis was broad but had many errors and inconsistencies: for example, in Grand Ancestor's second year of Tianxing Yao Xing changed his reign title, but Hong placed the change in the first year;
