translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong's synthesis was broad but had many errors and inconsistencies. For example, in Grand Ancestor's second year of Tianxing Yao Xing changed his reign title, but Hong placed the change in the first year;

sentences.zh: 太宗永興二年，慕容超擒於廣固，鴻又以為事在元年；

translations.literal: In Emperor Taizong's second year of Yongxing Murong Chao was captured at Guanggu, but Hong again placed the event in the first year;
translations.idiomatic: in Emperor Taizong's second year of Yongxing Murong Chao was captured at Guanggu, but Hong again placed the event in the first year;

sentences.zh: 太常二年，姚泓敗於長安，而鴻亦以為滅在元年。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taichang, Yao Hong was defeated at Chang'an, but Hong again placed the extinction in the first year.
translations.idiomatic: in the second year of Taichang, Yao Hong was defeated at Chang'an, but Hong again placed the extinction in the first year.

sentences.zh: 如此之失，多不考正。

translations.literal: Errors such as these were largely left uncorrected.
translations.idiomatic: Errors such as these were largely left uncorrected.

sentences.zh: 子子元，祕書郎。

translations.literal: His son Ziyuan, Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ziyuan served as Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 後永安中，乃奏其父書，曰：「臣亡考故散騎常侍、給事黃門侍郎、前將軍、齊州大中正鴻，不殞家風，式纘世業，古學克明，在新必鏡，多識前載，博極羣書，史才富洽，號稱籍甚。

translations.literal: Later in the Yongan era, he memorialized his father's book, saying: "My deceased father, the former Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Attendant Serving at the Yellow Gate, General of the Van, and Chief Rectifier of Qi Province, Hong, did not destroy the family tradition, continued the hereditary enterprise, mastered ancient learning, mirrored the new, knew much of former records, exhaustively mastered all books, had abundant historical talent, and was renowned and greatly famed.
translations.idiomatic: Later in the Yongan era, he memorialized his father's book, saying: "My deceased father, the former Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, Attendant Serving at the Yellow Gate, General of the Van, and Chief Rectifier of Qi Province, Cui Hong, did not destroy the family tradition but continued its hereditary work. He mastered ancient learning and mirrored the new, knew former records well, and exhaustively mastered all books. His historical talent was abundant, and his fame was great.

sentences.zh: 年止壯立，便斐然懷著述意。

translations.literal: While still only in the prime of manhood, he splendidly harbored intent to compose and record.
translations.idiomatic: While still only in the prime of manhood, he already splendidly harbored the intent to compose and record.

sentences.zh: 正始之末，任屬記言，撰緝餘暇，乃刊著趙、燕、秦、夏、涼、蜀等遺載，為之贊序，褒貶評論。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhenshi, entrusted with record-keeping, in spare moments from compilation he edited and published surviving records of Zhao, Yan, Qin, Xia, Liang, Shu, and others, writing prefaces for them with praise, blame, and commentary.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhenshi, entrusted with record-keeping, he used spare moments from compilation to edit and publish surviving records of Zhao, Yan, Qin, Xia, Liang, Shu, and others, writing prefaces with praise, blame, and commentary.

sentences.zh: 先朝之日，草構悉了，唯有李雄蜀書，搜索未獲，闕茲一國，遲留未成。

translations.literal: During the former reign, the draft structure was all complete; only the Shu book on Li Xiong was sought without finding; lacking this one state, completion was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: During the former reign the draft structure was complete, but only the Shu book on Li Xiong could not be found despite searching. Lacking this one state, the work remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 去正光三年，購訪始得，討論適訖，而先臣棄世。

translations.literal: When it reached the third year of Zhengguang, through purchase and inquiry it was finally obtained; discussion had just finished when my late father passed from the world.
translations.idiomatic: When the third year of Zhengguang arrived, it was finally obtained through purchase and inquiry. Discussion had just finished when my late father passed away.

sentences.zh: 凡十六國，名為春秋，一百二卷，近代之事最為備悉。

translations.literal: In all sixteen states, titled Spring and Autumn, one hundred and two fascicles—the affairs of recent times are most fully detailed.
translations.idiomatic: In all it covers sixteen states, titled Spring and Autumn, in one hundred and two fascicles, and the affairs of recent times are treated with the greatest fullness.

sentences.zh: 未曾奏上，弗敢宣流。

translations.literal: It had never been submitted to the throne; he did not dare circulate it publicly.
translations.idiomatic: It had never been submitted to the throne, and he did not dare circulate it publicly.

sentences.zh: 今繕寫一本，敢以仰呈。

translations.literal: Now I have copied one fascicle and venture to present it respectfully.
translations.idiomatic: Now I have copied one fascicle and venture to present it respectfully.

sentences.zh: 儻或淺陋，不回睿賞，乞藏祕閣，以廣異家。

translations.literal: If perchance it is shallow and crude and fails to win your sagacious approval, I beg that it be kept in the secret archive to broaden alternative accounts.
translations.idiomatic: If perchance it is shallow and crude and fails to win your sagacious approval, I beg that it be kept in the secret archive to broaden alternative accounts.

sentences.zh: 」子元後謀反，事發逃竄，會赦免。

translations.literal: " Later Ziyuan plotted rebellion; when the affair came to light he fled, but met with an amnesty and was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: " Later Ziyuan plotted rebellion. When the affair came to light he fled, but met with an amnesty and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 尋為其叔鵾所殺。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was killed by his uncle Kun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was killed by his uncle Kun.

sentences.zh: 光從祖弟長文，字景翰。

translations.literal: Guang's collateral cousin Changwen, courtesy name Jinghan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang's collateral cousin Changwen, courtesy name Jinghan.

sentences.zh: 少亦徙於代都，聰敏有學識。

translations.literal: In youth he also was moved to the capital at Dai; he was bright, clever, and possessed learning.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he too was moved to the capital at Dai. He was bright, clever, and well learned.

sentences.zh: 太和中，除奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, he was appointed Companion for the Court.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he was appointed court companion.

sentences.zh: 遷洛，拜司空參軍事，營構華林園。

translations.literal: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he was appointed Aide to the Minister of Works and constructed the Hualin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital moved to Luoyang, he was appointed aide to the Minister of Works and oversaw construction of the Hualin Garden.

sentences.zh: 後兼員外散騎常侍，為宕昌使主。

translations.literal: Later he concurrently served as Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary and as chief envoy to Dangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Later he concurrently served as supernumerary regular attendant-in-ordinary and as chief envoy to Dangchang.

sentences.zh: 還，授給事中、本國中正、尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: On his return, he was granted Attendant-in-Ordinary, Chief Rectifier of his native commandery, and Master in the Stores Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was granted attendant-in-ordinary, chief rectifier of his native commandery, and master in the Stores Bureau of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 正始中，大修器械，為諸州造仗都使。

translations.literal: In Zhenshi, when weapons were greatly repaired, he served as Director-in-Chief for forging arms for all provinces.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenshi, when weapons were greatly repaired, he served as director-in-chief for forging arms for all provinces.

sentences.zh: 齊州太原太守、雍州撫軍府長史，以廉慎稱。

translations.literal: Governor of Taiyuan in Qi Province and Chief Administrator of the Pacification Army headquarters in Yong Province; he was praised for integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Taiyuan in Qi Province and chief administrator of the Pacification Army headquarters in Yong Province, he was praised for integrity and prudence.

sentences.zh: 遷輔國將軍、中散大夫，轉太府少卿，丞相、高陽王雍諮議參軍，太中大夫。

translations.literal: Promoted to General Who Supports the State and Grand Master of the Palace; transferred to Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse, Advisory Aide to the Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, and Grand Master for All.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to general who supports the state and grand master of the palace, then transferred to vice director of the Imperial Storehouse, advisory aide to the Chancellor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, and grand master for all.

sentences.zh: 永安中，以老拜征虜將軍、平州刺史。

translations.literal: In Yongan, because of age he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Governor of Ping Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongan, because of his age he was appointed general who pacifies the barbarians and governor of Ping Province.

sentences.zh: 還家專讀佛經，不關世事。

translations.literal: Returning home, he devoted himself to reading Buddhist scriptures and paid no heed to worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home, he devoted himself to reading Buddhist scriptures and paid no heed to worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 年七十九，天平初卒。

translations.literal: At the age of seventy-nine, he died at the beginning of the Tianping era.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-nine at the beginning of the Tianping era.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、征東將軍、齊州刺史，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Bearer of the Staff of Authority, General Who Pacifies the East, and Governor of Qi Province; his posthumous name was Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was granted bearer of the staff of authority, general who pacifies the east, and governor of Qi Province, with the posthumous name Pure.

sentences.zh: 子慈懋，字德林。

translations.literal: His son Cimao, courtesy name Delin.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cimao, courtesy name Delin.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，征虜將軍、徐州征東府長史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi, General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Chief Administrator of the Eastern Expedition headquarters in Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi he served as general who pacifies the barbarians and chief administrator of the Eastern Expedition headquarters in Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 長文從弟庠，字文序。

translations.literal: Changwen's younger cousin Ku, courtesy name Wenxu.
translations.idiomatic: Changwen's younger cousin Ku, courtesy name Wenxu.

sentences.zh: 有幹用。

translations.literal: He was capable and effective.
translations.idiomatic: He was capable and effective.

sentences.zh: 初除侍御史、員外散騎侍郎、給事中。

translations.literal: Initially appointed Censor, Supernumerary Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He was initially appointed censor, supernumerary regular attendant-in-ordinary, and attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 頻使高麗，轉步兵校尉，又轉司空掾，領左右直長。

translations.literal: He frequently served as envoy to Goguryeo; transferred to Commandant of Footsoldiers, then to Aide to the Minister of Works, concurrently serving as Chief of the Left and Right Direct Attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He frequently served as envoy to Goguryeo, was transferred to commandant of footsoldiers, then to aide to the Minister of Works, and concurrently served as chief of the left and right direct attendants.

sentences.zh: 出除相州長史，還，拜河陰、洛陽令，以強直稱。

translations.literal: Sent out as Chief Administrator of Xiang Province; on return appointed Magistrate of Heyin and Luoyang, famed for firm uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as chief administrator of Xiang Province, and on his return was appointed magistrate of Heyin and Luoyang, famed for firm uprightness.

sentences.zh: 遷東郡太守。

translations.literal: Promoted to Governor of Dong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to governor of Dong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 元顥寇逼郡界，庠拒不從命，棄郡走還鄉里。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao raided the commandery borders, Ku refused to obey orders, abandoned the commandery, and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao raided the commandery borders, Ku refused to obey orders, abandoned the commandery, and fled home.

sentences.zh: 孝莊還宮，賜爵平原伯，拜潁川太守。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Ku was granted the noble rank of Baron of Pingyuan and appointed Governor of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang returned to the palace, Ku was granted the noble rank of baron of Pingyuan and appointed governor of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 二年五月，為城民王早、蘭寶等所害。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year, he was killed by city residents Wang Zao, Lan Bao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he was killed by city residents Wang Zao, Lan Bao, and others.

sentences.zh: 後贈驃騎將軍、吏部尚書、齊州刺史。

translations.literal: Later posthumously granted General of Agile Cavalry, Minister of Civil Appointments, and Governor of Qi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously granted general of agile cavalry, minister of civil appointments, and governor of Qi Province.

sentences.zh: 子罕襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Han inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, [his rank] was reduced according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, his rank was reduced according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 光族弟榮先，字隆祖，涉歷經史。

translations.literal: Guang's clansman Rongxian, courtesy name Longzu, broadly traversed the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang's clansman Rongxian, courtesy name Longzu, had broadly studied the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 州辟主簿。

translations.literal: The province recruited him as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The province recruited him as chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 子鐸，有文才。

translations.literal: His son Duo had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duo had literary talent.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Champion General and Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He served as champion general and grand master of the palace.

sentences.zh: 鐸弟覲，寧遠將軍、羽林監。

translations.literal: Duo's younger brother Jin, General of Distant Pacification and Supervisor of the Feathered Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Duo's younger brother Jin served as general of distant pacification and supervisor of the feathered guard.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：崔光風素虛遠，學業淵長。

translations.literal: The historiographer writes: Cui Guang's bearing was plain and remote, his learning deep and long.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Cui Guang's bearing was plain and remote, and his learning deep and broad.

sentences.zh: 高祖歸其才博，許其大至，明主固知臣也。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu credited his broad talent and granted him the highest rank—a wise lord indeed knows his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu credited his broad talent and granted him the highest rank—a wise lord indeed knows his ministers.

sentences.zh: 歷事三朝，師訓少主，不出宮省，坐致台傅，斯亦近世之所希有。

translations.literal: Serving three reigns, instructing the young lord, never leaving the palace precincts, yet attaining by sitting the rank of secretariat mentor—this too is rare in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Serving three reigns, instructing the young lord, never leaving the palace precincts, yet attaining the rank of secretariat mentor while sitting in place—this too is rare in recent times.

sentences.zh: 但顧懷大雅，託迹中庸，其於容身之譏，斯乃胡廣所不免也。

translations.literal: But looking to the great virtue and anchoring himself in the middle way, as for the reproach of self-preservation, this too Hu Guang could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: But in looking to the great virtue and anchoring himself in the middle way, the reproach of self-preservation was one that even Hu Guang could not escape.

sentences.zh: 鴻博綜古今，立言為事，亦才志之士乎？

translations.literal: Hong's synthesis ranged broadly through ancient and modern; establishing words as his enterprise—is he not also a man of talent and purpose?
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hong's synthesis ranged broadly through ancient and modern, and he made establishing words his life's work—is he not also a man of talent and purpose?

translations.idiomatic: Textual notes

sentences.zh: 后猶御武帷以接羣臣 冊府卷三二六

translations.literal: The empress still received the multitude of ministers behind a martial curtain: Cefu juan 326
translations.idiomatic: "The empress still received the multitude of ministers behind a martial curtain": Cefu, juan 326

sentences.zh: 〈三八六一頁〉

translations.literal: 〈page 3861〉
"Curtain" is written as "canopy."
translations.idiomatic: reads "curtain" as "canopy."

sentences.zh: 按事見漢書卷六八霍光傳，也作「帳」，疑「帷」字訛。

translations.literal: Commentary: the affair appears in Hanshu juan 68, biography of Huo Guang, which also reads "canopy"; suspect the character "curtain" is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the affair appears in Hanshu juan 68, biography of Huo Guang, which also reads "canopy"; "curtain" is likely a corruption.

sentences.zh: 或其事也 諸本「或」作「惑」。

translations.literal: Perhaps it was this affair: in various editions "or" is written as "confused."
translations.idiomatic: "Perhaps it was this affair": various editions read "or" as "confused."

translations.idiomatic: Beishi juan 44, biography of Cui Guang, and Cefu

translations.idiomatic: read as "or."

sentences.zh: 按冊府出魏書而與北史合，知魏書本亦作「或」，今據改。

translations.literal: Commentary: Cefu derives from the Book of Wei and agrees with Beishi; thus the Wei text also read "or"; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Cefu derives from the Book of Wei and agrees with Beishi, so the Wei text also read "or"; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 易本山泉 諸本「泉」作「火」，冊府卷六０三

translations.literal: The Changes: "Below the mountain is a spring": in various editions "spring" is written as "fire"; Cefu juan 603
translations.idiomatic: "The Changes: below the mountain is a spring": various editions read "spring" as "fire"; Cefu, juan 603

translations.literal: 〈page 7240〉

sentences.zh: 作「泉」。

translations.literal: Read as "spring."
translations.idiomatic: read as "spring."

sentences.zh: 按「山下出泉」，見易蒙象辭，「火」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Commentary: "Below the mountain a spring emerges" appears in the Image Commentary to the Hexagram Meng in the Changes; the character "fire" is erroneous; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "Below the mountain a spring emerges" appears in the Image Commentary to the Hexagram Meng in the Changes; "fire" is a corruption; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 孟子□實 冊府

translations.literal: Mencius □ shi: Cefu
translations.idiomatic: "Mencius □ shi": Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: 〈same juan and page as above〉
translations.idiomatic: (same juan and page as above)

sentences.zh: 闕字作「覈」。

translations.literal: The missing character is supplied as "he."
translations.idiomatic: The lacuna is supplied as "he."

sentences.zh: 按「覈實」語不見孟子，或是用盡心下「盡信書則不如無書，吾於武成取二三策而已」語意，但無確證，今不補。

translations.literal: Commentary: the phrase "he shi" does not appear in Mencius; it may draw on the sense of "If one fully trusts books, it is better to have no books; from the Completion of War I take only two or three strips" in Exerting the Mind, Part B, but there is no certain proof; not supplemented now.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the phrase "he shi" does not appear in Mencius. It may draw on the sense of "If one fully trusts books, it is better to have no books; from the Completion of War I take only two or three strips" in Exerting the Mind, Part B, but there is no certain proof; not supplemented.

sentences.zh: 基蹠泥灰 諸本「蹠」作「蹗」，冊府卷六０三

translations.literal: Foundation treading in mud and ash: in various editions "tread" is written as "lu"; Cefu juan 603
translations.idiomatic: "Foundation treading in mud and ash": various editions read "tread" as "lu"; Cefu, juan 603

translations.literal: 〈page 7240〉

sentences.zh: 作「蹠」。

translations.literal: Read as "tread."
translations.idiomatic: read as "tread."

sentences.zh: 按「蹗」是行貌，「基蹗」無義。

translations.literal: Commentary: "lu" denotes a manner of walking; "foundation lu" has no meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Note: "lu" denotes a manner of walking; "foundation lu" makes no sense.

sentences.zh: 「蹠」是履踐，「基蹠」猶言「基趾」，今據改。

translations.literal: "Tread" means to tread upon; "foundation tread" is like saying "foundation toe"; now emended accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: "Tread" means to tread upon; "foundation tread" is like "foundation toe"; emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 上酎祭宗廟出欲御樓船 諸本無「宗」字，冊府卷三二六

translations.idiomatic: "After the autumn libation sacrifice at the ancestral temple, going out intending to mount the tower ship": various editions lack the character "ancestral"; Cefu, juan 326

sentences.zh: 按漢書卷七一薛廣德傳作「宗廟」，「宗」字不宜省，今補。

translations.literal: Commentary: Hanshu juan 71, biography of Xue Guangde, reads "ancestral temple"; the character "ancestral" should not be omitted; now supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Note: Hanshu juan 71, biography of Xue Guangde, reads "ancestral temple"; the character "ancestral" should not be omitted; now supplemented.

sentences.zh: 又冊府「出」下有「便門」二字，與漢書合，但無此二字亦通，今不補。

translations.literal: Further, Cefu after "going out" has the two characters "Bian Gate," agreeing with Hanshu, but the passage is intelligible without these two characters; not supplemented now.
translations.idiomatic: Further, Cefu after "going out" has the two characters "Bian Gate," agreeing with Hanshu, but the passage is intelligible without them; not supplemented.

sentences.zh: 豈左右臣妾各竭虔仰 諸本「臣」字缺，今據冊府

translations.literal: How could the attendants left and right, ministers and concubines, each exhaust reverent devotion: in various editions the character "minister" is missing; now supplemented according to Cefu
translations.idiomatic: "How could the attendants left and right, ministers and concubines, each exhaust reverent devotion": various editions lack the character "minister"; now supplemented according to Cefu

sentences.zh: 歷員外郎騎侍郎 張森楷云：「上『郎』字疑當作『散』。

translations.literal: Served as Supernumerary Lang Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary. Zhang Senkai says: "The character lang above is probably a corruption of san."
translations.idiomatic: "Served as supernumerary lang cavalry attendant-in-ordinary": Zhang Senkai says, "The character lang above is probably a corruption of san."

sentences.zh: 」按「騎侍郎」上必當有「散」字。

translations.literal: " Commentary: above "Cavalry Attendant-in-Ordinary" there must originally have been the character "san."
translations.idiomatic: Note: above "cavalry attendant-in-ordinary" there must originally have been the character "san."

sentences.zh: 下載崔勵後官「散騎侍郎」，前是「員外」，後遷正，亦合。

translations.literal: Below it records Cui Li's later office as "Regular Attendant-in-Ordinary of Scattered Cavalry"; before he was "supernumerary," later promoted to regular rank—this also fits.
translations.idiomatic: Below it records Cui Li's later office as "regular attendant-in-ordinary of scattered cavalry." Before he was "supernumerary," and later was promoted to regular rank—this also fits.

sentences.zh: 上「郎」字當是「散」之訛。

translations.idiomatic: The preceding character "lang" should be a corruption of "san."
